title: Periphyton plays a dual role in the bioavailability of organic phosphorus in aquatic environments
description: Publication date: September 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry, Volume 206 Author(s): Cong-min Wu, Ren-yong Shi, Yuan-chun Yu, Xin-yu Hu, Ernest Uwiringiyimana, Jiu-yu Li, Ren-kou Xu
abstract: Periphyton exhibits a high affinity for inorganic phosphorus (IP), underscoring its importance as a sink in wetland phosphorus cycling. However, its role in regulating the biogeochemical cycling of organic phosphorus (OP) at the water-sediment interface remains underexplored. To address this gap, incubation experiments coupled with FTIR, XRD, and XPS analyses were conducted to investigate the effect of periphyton on OP bioavailability by exploring its capacity and mechanisms to hydrolyze and immobilize two representative OP compounds: glycerol phosphate (GP) and myo-inositol hexakisphosphate (IHP). In a 48-h dynamic incubation experiment with 0.4 g L−1 periphyton, the hydrolysis efficiency of GP reached 97% under light conditions and 63% in darkness. The enhanced GP hydrolysis was primarily driven by alkaline phosphatase secreted by periphyton, while abiotic hydrolysis mediated by iron/manganese oxides attached to periphyton played a secondary role. Under light conditions, periphyton elevated pH via photosynthesis (pH > 9), which further enhanced GP hydrolysis and simultaneously promoted precipitation of hydrolyzed IP into hydroxyapatite. In contrast, IHP hydrolysis was limited, mainly due to alkaline inhibition of phytase activity and substrate limitation from its rapid immobilization by periphyton. IHP underwent strong immobilization primarily through co-precipitation as calcium phytate, whereas surface complexation with iron oxides associated with periphyton was minimal. These results provide comprehensive mechanistic evidence that periphyton plays a dual biogeochemical role: promoting the hydrolysis of labile OP to increase phosphorus bioavailability, while simultaneously increasing pH through photosynthesis to facilitate sequestration of recalcitrant OP and hydrolyzed IP. Such findings provide valuable insights for phosphorus management in eutrophication-prone aquatic ecosystems.

title: Basalt glass alteration and phyllosilicate-type aluminosilicate development in the Lonar impact crater: Integrated mineralogical and geochemical evidence
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry, Volume 205 Author(s): M.R. Singh, N. Ragde, R. Ragde
abstract: The Lonar Crater, a closed-basin alkaline lake developed within Deccan basalt, preserves sediments undergoing accelerated alteration of impact-generated basaltic glass under evaporative, low-drainage conditions. Five representative lake-bed samples (L1–L5) were analysed using X-ray diffraction (XRD) within the measurable angular range (10–90° 2θ), FTIR–ATR spectroscopy, SEM–EDS, XRF, helium pycnometry, and TGA–DTG to constrain the evolution of crystalline, amorphous, carbonate, and Fe-oxide phases. Although the absence of sub-10° reflections precludes definitive identification of basal (00l) spacings for clay minerals, complementary indicators—including broadened Si–O and O–H FTIR bands, platy to fine-grained microtextures observed in SEM, and dehydroxylation signals between 500 and 560 °C—collectively support the presence of hydroxyl-bearing aluminosilicate phases derived from hydrated basaltic glass. Estimated crystallite sizes (∼35–70 nm) further suggest the presence of nanophase mineral components. Spatial variations in carbonate peak intensity, Fe-oxide abundance, and amorphous-phase expression define three compositional components across the lake floor, reflecting gradients in pH, water residence time, and redox conditions. These results demonstrate that Lonar functions as a hydrochemically confined alteration system capable of generating clay-sized alteration products and authigenic carbonates from basaltic substrates. The mineralogical parallels with alteration suites reported from Martian crater-lake deposits suggest that Lonar may serve as a process-based terrestrial analogue for interpreting basalt weathering, diagenesis, and carbon sequestration pathways in restricted lacustrine environments on Earth and other planetary bodies.

title: Geochemical associations and local prediction of rare earth elements in fine-grained stream and pond sediments from agricultural catchments (SW France)
description: Publication date: Available online 24 May 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry Author(s): Xinda Wu, Cheng Gu, Anne Probst
abstract: Rare earth elements (REE) are attracting increasing attention as indispensable materials and emerging micropollutants, yet their behavior in carbonate-rich agricultural sediments remains poorly understood. This study investigated REE concentrations and physicochemical properties in the fine fraction (<63 μm) of stream and pond sediments from three agricultural catchments in the Save Basin, southwestern France: Montoussé (MON), Mican (MIC), and Nuguet (NUG). Light rare earth elements (LREE) dominated total REE (TREE) concentrations, ranging from 108.13 to 182.12 mg kg-1, whereas heavy rare earth elements (HREE) exhibited lower concentrations (11.33–17.23 mg kg-1). Although LREE and HREE were strongly correlated, their spatial patterns differed, with LREE varying significantly among catchments and HREE tending to be higher in pond than in stream sediments. Multivariate and controlled analyses showed a robust negative association between calcium (Ca) and both LREE and HREE, consistent with carbonate-related dilution, whereas the positive Al-HREE association was weaker and more context dependent. PAAS-normalized patterns were generally smooth, and median Ce/Ce* (1.035) and Eu/Eu* (1.039) remained close to unity, supporting predominantly lithogenic background and carbonate-related dilution rather than strong element-specific anthropogenic anomalies. Local empirical models for LREE and HREE were evaluated using Ca and Al as readily measurable proxies. TREE concentrations decreased along the stream-flow direction, consistent with carbonate enrichment in downstream pond sediments. These results highlight the importance of carbonate-rich sediment composition and pond-scale sediment retention for interpreting REE behavior in agricultural sediments.

title: Processes affecting pollution fluxes during the coastal erosion of legacy colliery wastes
description: Publication date: Available online 23 May 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry Author(s): Ian T. Burke, Sebastian J. Pitman, James Hodson, Lin Niu, Fatmah Mohammed, Jenni Ilari Skakunova, Alex L. Riley, Catherine J. Gandy, Elliot Whitehead, Karen A. Hudson-Edwards, Elin Jennings, Helen Jay, Nick Cooper, Adam P. Jarvis, William M. Mayes
abstract: The fate and behaviour of legacy coastal waste deposits are of concern due to the potential for future climate change to increase contaminant fluxes from these sources. During the 20th century 39-47 million m3 of pyritic colliery spoil was dumped onto beaches in County Durham, Northeast England. Distribution of this waste along the coastline produced a 4-6 m high compacted colliery spoil terrace, which extended around 200 m seaward of original shoreline. After the cessation of tipping between 1974 and 1993, ongoing erosion of spoil terraces at these sites has become a source of several potentially toxic elements (PTEs) to coastal ecosystems. The compacted spoil material had an in-situ bulk density of 1.8 (1.2-2.0) t m-3 and moisture content of 21 (11-31) wt. % and contained potentially problematic mean concentrations of As (142 mg kg-1), Ba (1300 mg kg-1), Hg (0.63 mg kg-1), Pb (154 mg kg-1), and Zn (111 mg kg-1). Leaching tests showed that the remobilisation of these PTEs was low across a range of pH, indicating particulate dispersion as the most important pollutant transport mechanism at these sites. However, particle winnowing and density separation occur during spoil erosion. Fe oxide and pyrite grains from the spoil were preferentially retained in adjacent fine sand intertidal sediments, which as a result, also contained high concentrations of PTEs. Analysis of beach volume changes between 2010 and 2023 revealed that approximately 500,000 m3 of spoil was removed by coastal erosion in this period. This equates to median annual fluxes of As (6.6 t yr-1), Hg (0.027 t yr-1), and Pb (4.6 t yr-1), and Zn (4.5 t yr-1) which are not trivial when compared to annual fluxes from permitted UK industrial discharges or metal mine discharges in England and Wales. The high flux of As is particularly of concern due to the lack of other significant local sources of this metalloid in Northeast England. Although >95 % of the originally tipped spoil has already been dispersed offshore, approximately 1 million m3 of spoil is currently still present in beach deposits, which will remain a significant source of PTEs to coastal environments for several more decades.

title: Integrative source identification of heavy metal(loid)s in agricultural soils of a geologically diverse and anthropogenically impacted urban area along the lower Yangtze River, Eastern China
description: Publication date: Available online 22 May 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry Author(s): Xiaodan Cui, Jun Tu, Shunsheng Huang, Peiliang He, Jie Liu, Zhiying Guo, Biao Huang
abstract: In the economically developed and densely populated lower Yangtze River region, urbanization and industrialization have led to the accumulation of heavy metal(loid)s (HMs) in agricultural soils, posing potential risks to human health. This study selected Nanjing, a typical city in this area, and collected 204 surface soil samples to systematically investigate the concentrations, distribution, enrichment status, and sources of HMs. The results showed that the average concentrations of most HMs (except Cd and Ni) were elevated relative to the corresponding background values. According to the single-factor pollution index, Cu and Hg exhibited the highest pollution levels, followed by Cd and Ni; however, the overall pollution level of the region was low, with 87.7% of samples classified as “no pollution”. Spatial distribution revealed that most HMs shared similar hotspot patterns along the banks of the Yangtze River, while soil samples from basalt outcrop areas showed higher concentrations of Cr, Ni, and Mn. Both pollution hotspots and elevated ecological risk were mainly distributed in the major industrial zones and urbanizing suburbs, with Qixia District dominated by Cd and Cu, and Jiangning and Lishui Districts dominated by Hg. Through principal component analysis (PCA) and positive matrix factorization (PMF), four sources were identified and quantified: basalt weathering (54.1%), characterized by Cr, Ni, and Mn and highly correlated with basalt outcrop areas; Yangtze River alluvium (25.5%), enriched in As, Cd, Pb, Zn, Sb, and Se and distributed along the Yangtze River, including Baguazhou; an industrial mixed source (11.8%), dominated by Cu, Cd, and Zn, including copper mining, metal smelting and processing activities; and an industrial and traffic source characterized by Hg (8.6%). This study clearly distinguished two natural sources by comprehensively considering regional geological diversity, providing an integrative approach for source apportionment of HMs in agricultural soils of cities along the lower Yangtze River, and contributing to the establishment of a differentiated “source identification-zoning-management” strategy.

title: Lithological controls on seasonal weathering processes in a non-glaciated lesser Himalayan spring system
description: Publication date: Available online 22 May 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry Author(s): Nitish Kumar, Om Kumar, Satyabrata Das, Abhayanad Singh Maurya
abstract: Chemical weathering in the Himalayan watershed acts as a natural laboratory and plays a crucial role in shaping the spring water chemistry. In this study, seasonal dissolved inorganic carbon isotope (δ13CDIC) and major ion data, coupled with multivariate analysis, were used to understand the role of acids in ongoing weathering processes and, ultimately, to identify the factors regulating spring water chemistry in the non-glaciated Takoli Gad watershed, Lesser Himalaya. The δ13CDIC of spring water shows significant seasonal variations, with the most enriched value during the monsoon season, followed by the winter season, and the premonsoon season, characterised by the most depleted values. Interpretation of δ13CDIC and major ions implies that carbonic acid-derived carbonate weathering is the main geochemical process that contributes to the solute fluxes. Additionally, seasonal recharge and anthropogenic activity play a significant role in defining spring water chemistry. The dominance of carbonate weathering in the watershed initiates a dual pathway: primarily short-term CO2 consumption via carbonic acid weathering, and only a minimal contribution from sulfuric acid-driven CO2 release. Insights gained from this study are crucial for a deeper understanding of carbon cycling, weathering patterns, and spring sustainability in the Lesser Himalayas.

title: Reconstructing Transitional Paleoredox Conditions from the Late Cretaceous Oceanic Anoxic Events 2 to 3 across Intracratonic Platform, Narmada Rift Basin, Central India
description: Publication date: Available online 20 May 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry Author(s): Prantik Mondal, Biplab Bhattacharya
abstract: Reconstructing Cretaceous redox evolution is vital to understanding climate–carbon cycle feedbacks during greenhouse intervals marked by Oceanic Anoxic Events (OAEs). While OAE2 is globally well recognized, the post-OAE2 to OAE3 transition (spanning ∼8 Myr) remains poorly constrained in intracratonic epicontinental settings. This study investigates the Nodular (Turonian) and Bryozoan (Coniacian) Limestone Formations within the intracratonic Narmada Basin, central India, to evaluate how global anoxic signals were expressed within a tectonically restricted rift segment of the Tethyan realm. A multi-proxy geochemical framework was employed to reconstruct paleoenvironmental dynamics, integrating redox-sensitive trace-element enrichment factors (EFs) and their ratios (U/Th, V/Cr, V/(V+Ni)), the salinity indicator (Sr/Ba), rare-earth-element systematics (∑REE+Y, Ce/Ce*, Eu/Eu*, Y/Ho, (Pr/Yb)N), stable isotopes (δ13C, δ18O, δ13C_org), and total organic carbon (TOC), was used to reconstruct paleoenvironmental dynamics. Results reveal a temporal progressive shift from mixed siliciclastic–carbonate to carbonate-dominated deposition, with declining terrigenous input and intensifying salinity and redox stratification. Eight discrete environmental perturbations (E1–E8 events) record basin-wide variability: the western, basin-distal part evolved into persistently dysoxic to anoxic conditions under fluctuating salinity, whereas the eastern, continent-proximal part remained comparatively well ventilated, receiving periodic freshwater influx. Events E5–E8 coincide with the global OAE3 interval (Coniacian), reflecting sustained anoxia under extreme salinity stratification. Importantly, unlike typical global OAE3 successions characterized by slight positive δ13C excursions linked to enhanced organic carbon burial. In contrast, the eastern Narmada Basin preserves anomalously negative carbonate δ13C values (–8‰ to 0‰), reflecting strong internal carbon recycling, driven by organic matter remineralization, microbial carbon fluxes, methane seepage, and volcanic inputs. This isotopic inversion underscores how restricted basins can overprint canonical OAE signatures through local hydrographic and biogeochemical feedbacks.

title: Thallium isotopic compositions reveal a significant contribution of thallium in soils from natural weathering processes
description: Publication date: Available online 20 May 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry Author(s): Yinyin Lu, Ruoxuan Qiu, Hangfei Guo, Dieyu Chen, Zicong Tan, Pei Li, Yurong Gao, Jin Wang, Juan Liu
abstract: Resultant thallium (Tl) enrichment in soils by anthropogenic mining activities of Hg-Tl ore has been well documented, yet the mechanism of Tl migration and redistribution in soils dominated by natural weathering process remains poorly understood. Herein, two representative soil profiles beyond the core mining zone of the world-class Lanmuchang Hg-Tl deposit, China were screened and analyzed by elemental and high-precision Tl isotopic measurements. The results show that thallium average concentrations in both profiles (A: 75.5 mg/kg; B: 43.3 mg/kg) are significantly higher than national background level in China (0.62 mg/kg). A three end-member mixing model for quantitative source apportionment indicated that the natural weathering and dispersion of lorandite (TlAsS2) constitute the dominant source of thallium enrichment in profiles A (65.40–94.83%) and B (45.02–72.05%), rather than from anthropogenic mining activities. Notably, Fe-bearing secondary minerals of jarosite and hematite acted as strong hosts for Tl and As, participating in the co-migration of both elements and driving the observed Tl isotopic fractionation. The study demonstrates that natural weathering process may induce highly enriched Tl concentration in soils whereas stable Tl isotopes can constrain relative contributions from geogenic and anthropogenic sources when applying a ternary mixing model.

title: Unravelling controls on carbon mineralization in fractures: Insights from 3D reactive transport simulations in olivine
description: Publication date: 5 September 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 717 Author(s): Lawrence O. Boampong, Alexander C. Murph, Jeffrey D. Hyman, Alexis Navarre-Sitchler, Hari S. Viswanathan
abstract: Carbon mineralization in mafic-ultramafic rocks is a promising pathway for long-term carbon dioxide (CO2) sequestration. While these rocks rely heavily on fractures for fluid flow and transport, the interplay between geochemical reactions, fracture network structure, and hydrology remains uncertain. Furthermore, three-dimensional models that explicitly resolve coupled dissolution–precipitation reactions within fracture networks relevant to carbon mineralization are rare. This study presents a three-dimensional modeling framework to investigate olivine mineralization in fractured media. Fracture networks were generated using dfnWorks, and flow and reactive transport was simulated with PFLOTRAN. A sensitivity analysis was performed to evaluate the influence of various controlling factors on the mineralization amount. Results reveal that factors controlling mineralization are highly dynamic and context dependent. Temperature dominates mineralization at early reaction stages, reflecting kinetic control of dissolution and cation release. As precipitation progresses, transport limitations emerge, and injection volumetric flow rate and fracture aperture become the primary drivers of extent of mineralization. For maximum mineralization outcomes, dominant parameters differ by system complexity. Porosity and injection volumetric flow rate dominates in single fracture, while aperture, temperature, and injection volumetric flow rate control mineralization in fracture networks. These findings provide a framework for understanding how carbon mineralization evolves in fractured systems and offer guidance for interpreting variability in mineralization behavior under different geochemical and hydrodynamic conditios.

title: Organic matter and seasonal flooding control mercury and methane distribution in sediments of a floodplain lake in the Madeira River basin (western Amazon)
description: Publication date: Available online 23 May 2026 Source: Chemical Geology Author(s): Yara Paole Lopes de Paiva Sodré, Lucas Cabrera Monteiro, Cláudio Eduardo Azevedo-Silva, Ronaldo de Almeida, Claudio Cardoso Marinho, Jeremie Garnier, Ygor Oliveira Sarmento Rodrigues, Wanderley Rodrigues Bastos, José Vicente Elias Bernardi
abstract: We investigated the spatial distribution and environmental controls of total Hg (THg), methane (CH4), and nutrient accumulation in the sediments of an Amazonian lake during low-water and high-water periods. THg concentrations were similar between hydrological periods (0.103 ± 0.035 mg kg−1 in low water; 0.104 ± 0.039 mg kg−1 in high water) and were consistently associated with organic matter (TOC) and nitrogen (N). In contrast, CH4 exhibited strong seasonal variability, with significantly higher concentrations during high water (7.94 ± 4.35 mg kg−1) compared to low water (4.43 ± 3.05 mg kg−1). Phosphorus (P) and water depth also increased markedly during high water, reflecting enhanced hydrological connectivity. Geostatistical analyses revealed that THg, TOC, and N shared similar spatial patterns, with higher concentrations in central and distal portions of the lake, whereas CH4 was more spatially variable. Generalized least squares models indicated that THg was primarily controlled by TOC and pH during low water and by N during high water, whereas CH4 was influenced by TOC in low water and by N and water depth in high water. Spatial congruence between THg and TOC (54.1%) and between THg and N (51.7%) was moderate, increasing substantially under relaxed criteria (>93%). Methane showed weaker spatial correspondence with its predictors. These results demonstrate that hydrological seasonality decouples Hg and CH4 dynamics, with Hg strongly linked to organic matter and CH4 responding to shifts in nutrient availability and water column conditions.

title: Transition from subduction initiation to mature subduction: Geochemical evidence from Cenozoic mafic-felsic intrusive rocks, Central Philippines
description: Publication date: Available online 22 May 2026 Source: Chemical Geology Author(s): Yu Wang, Xiaoyong Yang, Jianghong Deng, Linzi Li, Chuhan Fan, Russyl Lanzaderas, Weidong Sun
abstract: The Philippine Mobile Belt records a complex Cenozoic subduction history, yet the subduction initiation processes during the Cenozoic and the characteristics of subsequent magmatic evolution remain poorly constrained. Here, we present the first integrated petrological, geochronological, and geochemical study of Eocene–Oligocene intrusive rocks from Bohol Island, central Philippines, including pyroxene diorite (44–41 Ma), medium-grained quartz diorite (39 Ma), and coarse-grained quartz diorite (35 Ma). The early pyroxene diorites are geochemically highly depleted with N-MORB-like REE distribution patterns but much lower REE contents, which resemble the geochemical characteristics of forearc basalts that are formed during the initial subduction stage. Furthermore, the enrichment of fluid-mobile elements such as high Pb, Sr, Rb, Ba, U, and K of these rocks suggests that more slab-derived fluids were added in the mantle source than those of forearc basalts. Combining the depleted Nd isotopes (εNd(t) = 8.28–9.16) but relatively enriched Sr isotopes (87Sr/86Sri = 0.703366–0.704565), we suggest the mafic intrusive rocks were formed by partial melting of a depleted mantle with the contribution of fluids from the altered oceanic crust during the early-stage subduction after subduction initiation. Furthermore, whole-rock Pb (208Pb/204Pbi = 37.9770–38.2556; 207Pb/204Pbi = 15.4824–15.5659; 206Pb/204Pbi = 18.4860–18.5505) and Nd isotopes, and magmatic zircon Hf (εHf(t) = 10.7–18.8) isotopic compositions of these intrusive rocks reveal the contribution from fluids released by the subducted Pacific-type oceanic crust and partial melting of an Indian-type MORB mantle source. In contrast, the ca. 39–35 Ma quartz diorite suites are more felsic, showing more evolved geochemical characteristics, e.g., fractionated REE patterns and elevated Th contents, suggesting that more slab melt is added into the mantle. This indicates that the tectonic regime evolved from an incipient subduction to a more mature stage during this period. This study identified the magmatic records from incipient subduction to mature subduction in the Philippine Island Arc during the Cenozoic, providing further petrological and geochemical constraints on the Cenozoic subduction initiation and subsequent tectonic evolution on the western margin of the Philippine Sea Plate.

title: Nickel toxicity inhibits abundance and activity of cyanobacteria and Fe(III)-reducers in low-phosphate Archean oceans
description: Publication date: Available online 21 May 2026 Source: Chemical Geology Author(s): Carolin L. Dreher, Manuel Schad, Kurt O. Konhauser, Andreas Kappler
abstract: Banded iron formations (BIFs) are iron (Fe)- and silica (SiO2)-rich marine chemical sediments that formed between 3.8 and 1.85 Ga, recording early ocean geochemistry and the rise of oxygen during the Great Oxidation Event (GOE, ~2.45 Ga). Cyanobacterial oxygen (O2) production led to iron mineral precipitation, with subsequent Fe(III) reduction by dissimilatory Fe(III)-reducing bacteria (DIRB). However, the remobilization and roles of essential dissolved nutrients (phosphate, PO4 3−) and micronutrients that also function as potential toxins (nickel, Ni), remain unclear. We conducted batch experiments with two consecutive Fe(II) oxidation and Fe(III) reduction cycles with the marine cyanobacterium Synechococcus sp. PCC7002 and the DIRB Shewanella colwelliana under simulated Archean ocean conditions (0.5 mM Fe2+ aq, 0.67 mM SiO2 aq) with varying concentrations of PO4 3− (3.67 and 367 μM) and Ni (0.4, 4 and 40 μM). High Ni (4, 40 μM) inhibited growth, except at high PO4 3− (365 μM) with 4 μM Ni, whereas total cell counts temporarily increased from 2 × 107 cells/mL at day 60 to 6 × 107 cells/mL at day 135, followed by a decline to 4 × 107 cells/mL by day 195. Low PO4 3− concentrations (3.67 μM) limited growth except at low Ni (0.4 μM), rising from 2 × 107 cells/mL on day 60 to 8 × 107 cells/mL by day 82. These results suggest that first, the combined stress of high Ni toxicity and low PO4 3− availability likely constrained cyanobacterial proliferation, possibly delaying the onset of the GOE. Second, DIRB could remobilize PO4 3− during Fe(III) reduction, thereby sustaining microbial activity and maintaining iron cycling in the early ocean.

title: Quantitative PMF-based source apportionment of trace elements in spring and groundwater, coupled with thermodynamic modeling, solid-aqueous partitioning, and health-risk assessment
description: Publication date: Available online 21 May 2026 Source: Chemical Geology Author(s): Utpal Majee, R. Sreelesh, S. Ajith, Prasenjit Das, K. Sreelash, Shiekha E. John, K. Maya
abstract: Accurately resolving geogenic versus anthropogenic controls on trace-element mobility is important for assessing water quality in heterogeneous hydrogeological settings. This study integrates Positive Matrix Factorization (PMF), thermodynamic modeling (PHREEQC), and molar ratio diagnostics. It characterizes thermal and cold springs, and groundwaters (n = 68) across the lateritic, crystalline, basaltic, and sedimentary terrains of the western continental margins of India. Molar ratios help distinguish laterite-influenced regolith systems, feldspar-weathering dominated cold springs, and saline or thermal waters. PMF identifies three major source-related patterns: near-surface soil and laterite weathering, redox- related mobilization, and deep rock-water interaction or input from saline sources. Thermodynamic modeling suggests that acidic lateritic springs are close to saturation with gibbsite (SI ≈ −0.2), while monsoonal samples show supersaturation with ferrihydrite (SI > +1.4), indicating likely colloidal transport. Thermal springs (~41–69 °C) exhibit equilibrium conditions with calcite and barite, consistent with deeper circulation pathways. Partition coefficients (K d), from a sub-region indicate non-linear sorption in acidic lateritic aquifers. Proton competition drives strong inverse correlations for Zn and Ba (r > −0.7), suggesting limited buffering and greater mobility under acidic conditions. Enrichment patterns further distinguish natural geothermal LiB signatures from residual Ag enrichment in lateritic settings. Water pollution indices indicate low contamination and minimal health risk (HI < 1), except at one site where a monsoon-driven spike linked to Co and Fe, exceeding the children's risk threshold. Overall, the results suggest that these spring and groundwater systems are influenced by geochemical processes and may be sensitive to seasonal and future environmental perturbations.

title: Humic acid–mediated shift in •OH formation location enhances contaminant degradation during oxygenation of surface-adsorbed Fe(II)
description: Publication date: Available online 21 May 2026 Source: Chemical Geology Author(s): Wenwen Ji, Chenglong Yu, Yuying Tang, Benyin Zhou, Hanshuang Liu, Shengyan Pu
abstract: Hydroxyl radicals (•OH) generated during oxygenation of Fe(II)-bearing soils and sediments play an important role in the abiotic transformation of organic contaminants in redox-fluctuating subsurface environments. Adsorbed Fe(II) at mineral surfaces is considered the most reactive Fe(II) species for activating O2 to produce •OH. However, the influence of ubiquitous natural organic matter such as humic acids (HA) on •OH production and contaminant degradation remains unclear. Here, we show that the presence of HA decreased the oxidation rate of adsorbed Fe(II) and increased •OH production. The enhanced •OH yield resulted from a shift in reaction pathways from direct oxidation of adsorbed Fe(II) to oxidation of HA-complexed Fe(II). Electron transfer from Fe(II) to O2 is also mediated by quinone moieties in both adsorbed and dissolved HA. The modulation of the Fe coordination environment through the formation of Fe-HA complexes plays a more important role than HA-mediated electron shuttling in enhancing •OH production. Moreover, HA mediation shifted the location of •OH generation from the mineral surface to the bulk solution. As a result, HA increased the •OH utilization efficiency for phenol degradation by 2.1–2.3 times by decreasing •OH quenching at the mineral surface. Even though the addition of ESHA only slightly increased the total •OH production (< 8%), it still resulted in a pronounced enhancement in phenol degradation by 120–154%. These findings reveal an important but overlooked role of the •OH generation location in groundwater contaminant degradation and highlight the contribution of HA-mediated •OH production and contaminant transformation in organic matter rich soils and aquifers.

title: Optimizing a chemical cleaning protocol to determine the nickel isotopic composition of ancient seawater from carbonates
description: Publication date: Available online 21 May 2026 Source: Chemical Geology Author(s): Eva J. Baransky, MingZhao Sun, Laura E. Wasylenki
abstract: Reconstructing the ancient marine cycle of Ni, a trace metal in the oceans essential to enzymes regulating the C, N, and O cycles, would inform how Ni bioavailability shaped early life. The Ni isotopic composition of seawater (δ60NiSW) through time could provide insight, but this approach requires sedimentary archives that faithfully record δ60NiSW. Carbonates are an often-used record of seawater chemistry, but contaminants could bias the measured δ60Ni of bulk sediment. To isolate the true carbonate-bound δ60Ni signal, we optimized a chemical cleaning protocol designed to minimize non‑carbonate Ni contributions and maximize carbonate recovery. We analyzed ODP Site 1007 sediments and evaluated oxidative and reductive pre-cleaning steps and carbonate dissolution protocols. Our results show that only reductive cleaning significantly altered the subsequent carbonate leachate composition, lowering Ni/Ca ratios by up to 60% and δ60Ni values by as much as 0.4 ‰. In contrast, δ60Ni values were largely insensitive to premature carbonate dissolution during pre-cleaning or to partial leaching of silicates during carbonate dissolution, even at higher acid molarities or longer reaction times. We recommend an evidence-based protocol that removes hydro-soluble salts and clays, applies reductive cleaning and oxidative cleaning for certain sample compositions, and dissolves carbonate using 0.5 M acetic acid, adjusted to pH 5. Using these results, we infer a ∼ 0.9 ‰ Ni isotopic fractionation between chemically cleaned deep-water carbonates (+0.4 ± 0.1 ‰) and deep seawater. This method development is a key step toward accurately reconstructing ancient marine Ni cycles.

title: Accurate determination of the Mn(II), Mn(III), and Mn(IV) contents in Mn oxides using a modified pyrophosphate extraction method
description: Publication date: Available online 20 May 2026 Source: Chemical Geology Author(s): Yan Li, Lorenzo Spadini, Jianlin Liao, Armelle Crouzet, Matthieu Blanc, Romain Biron, Olivier Mathon, Alain Manceau
abstract: Redox properties of Mn oxides play a central role in metal cycling and material reactivity because of their variable Mn(II)/Mn(III)/Mn(IV) contents. Typical chemical methods estimate the Mn(II)/Mn(III)/Mn(IV) proportions by measuring Mn(III) with pyrophosphate (PP) and calculating the average manganese oxidation state (AMOS) using redox-based techniques. In this study, we introduce a modified PP method (MPP) that allows measuring each Mn oxidation state individually without requiring a separate AMOS measurement. Eight poorly crystallized birnessite (δ-MnO2), with different AMOS levels, were synthesized under various chemical conditions, including changes in pH, ionic strength, and reductant treatment. These samples were analyzed with X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectroscopy, the four most common redox-based methods, and the MPP method to evaluate their accuracy and precision. The redox methods, including oxalate back-titration, iodometry, potentiometry, and LBBI colorimetry, yielded inconsistent Mn(II)/Mn(III)/Mn(IV) proportions and AMOS values, with AMOS differences ranging from 0.15 to 0.78 across the four methods for the same sample. The AMOS values obtained with the MPP method agreed with those measured by XANES and potentiometry, and showed no agreement with those from the other three chemical methods. The MPP method provides higher precision for the Mn(II)/Mn(III)/Mn(IV) proportions of the eight δ-MnO2 samples (standard deviations, SD ≤ 0.01) compared to the four redox methods (SD up to 0.10). Since potentiometry and XANES are considered the most accurate methods for measuring AMOS, we conclude that the MPP method represents a significant advancement in quantifying Mn(II), Mn(III), and Mn(IV) in Mn oxides.

title: Dynamic capillary effects in layered porous media: dependence on flow direction and displacement front stability
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 676 Author(s): Xinang Xu, Yajuan Zhuang, Dingjiang Chen, Lingzao Zeng
abstract: Conventional static equilibrium models do not fully capture the coupling among transient interfacial dynamics, fluid viscosity, and pore-scale heterogeneity, which complicates the quantification of dynamic capillary effects and the identification of an appropriate quasi-static reference. To address these issues, we conducted microfluidic drainage experiments in oil-wet layered porous media and evaluated the use of interfacial-area-weighted capillary pressure as a quasi-static interfacial capillary reference. The non-equilibrium deviation was interpreted within a pressure-work-density framework and used to quantify the dynamic capillary coefficient τ. The results reveal a systematic directional dependence of the dynamic response: under favorable viscosity-ratio conditions, coarse-to-fine (CTF) displacement exhibits stronger non-equilibrium behavior, with τ values 30% to 175% higher than those in fine-to-coarse (FTC) displacement. This contrast suggests that structural constraints associated with the coarse–fine transition can outweigh interfacial-area effects under stable displacement conditions. We further show that displacement-front stability modulates how layered heterogeneity is expressed: stable fronts preserve the influence of permeability gradients, whereas unstable viscous fingering tends to mask directional characteristics associated with pore-scale asymmetry. Overall, these findings indicate that the dynamic coefficient depends not only on fluid properties and saturation, but also on flow directionality and pore structure, which has implications for developing predictive models that reduce upscaling bias in layered aquifers and remediation flushing.

title: Freshwater carbon sequestration in eutrophic reservoirs: Superior burial efficiency compared to coastal seagrass, marsh, and mangrove blue carbon habitats under global warming
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 676 Author(s): Yuening Peng, Keisuke Nakayama, Taketoshi Shimizu, Junpei Omori, Kohji Uno, Tomoyasu Fujii, Hao-Chi Lin, Jeng-Wei Tsai
abstract: Assessing “freshwater carbon” budgets is essential for mitigating global warming, yet carbon dynamics in eutrophic reservoirs remain poorly understood. This study investigated the Karasuhara Reservoir, a typical eutrophic system in Japan, using long-term data from two periods: 1982–1999 (“past”) and 2010–2018 (“present”). Our study centered on two key objectives: identifying the main drivers of reservoir DIC and evaluating how warming influences carbon burial mechanisms. By employing structural equation modeling (SEM), we revealed that river inflow, phytoplankton CO2 absorption, and dissolved organic carbon (DOC) mineralization are the primary drivers of dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) dynamics in the epilimnion. Our net ecosystem production model further quantified these temporal dynamics, demonstrating that DIC fluctuations are governed by the balance between phytoplankton uptake, DOC mineralization, and bottom-layer leaching. Although extended residence times (>200 days) and stable stratification facilitate carbon sequestration by inhibiting the upwelling of bottom waters; however, these favorable conditions are being undermined by global warming. Net carbon burial rates dropped significantly from a mean of 158 mg-C m–2 d–1 (1982–1999) to 101 mg-C m–2 d–1 (2010–2018), likely as increased water temperatures reduced photosynthetic activity. Despite this decline, the reservoir exhibited a high burial efficiency (57% to 68%), underscoring the pivotal yet temperature-sensitive role of eutrophic freshwater systems in global carbon sequestration. Leveraging a 35-year continuous monitoring record and an integrated SEM + process-based NEP modeling framework, this study provides a site-scale empirical attribution of how a + 1.1 °C inter-period warming corresponded to a − 57 mg-C m–2 d–1 change in net carbon burial in an under-represented ecosystem type — an enclosed temperate eutrophic reservoir.

title: Four decades of dissolved organic carbon dynamics in Lake Taihu using comprehensive Landsat-5/7/8 observations and advanced machine learning models with investigation on driving factors
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 676 Author(s): Feilong Shen, Jifeng Li, Tianwei Wang, Nian Li, Jiawei Yang, Mengyang Xu, Yange Yan, Linhuan He, Yulong Guo, Zhongbing Chen
abstract: Dissolved organic carbon (DOC) plays a crucial role in lake carbon cycling, yet its long-term variations and key drivers remain poorly understood, particularly in large eutrophic lakes. Using 40 years of Landsat data and four machine learning (ML) models, we reconstructed DOC concentration (DOCc) and storage (DOCs) in Lake Taihu for the whole lake (T0) and six open-water zones: Gonghu Bay (T1), Meiliang Bay (T2), Zhushan Bay (T3), Central Lake (T4), Northwest Lake (T5), and Southwest Lake (T6). The XGBoost model achieved high accuracy (validation: R2 = 0.73, RMSE = 0.51 mg/L, MAPE = 8.66%, RPD = 1.70), revealing spatiotemporal DOC variability (2.49–6.36 mg/L). DOCc peaked at 4.90 mg/L in 1996 and declined after 2000, with lower levels in several zones after 2010. Lake-wide DOCs showed interannual variability and a slight decrease, peaking at 16,906 t C in 2010 and showing a linear trend of −138.51 t C/decade. Regional differences highlight strong hydrodynamic flushing in T6 (−106.63 t C/decade), while localized increases in T1 and T5 may reflect nutrient-driven productivity and sedimentary carbon accumulation. Meteorological factors were the strongest direct controls on DOCc (−0.72) and DOCs (−0.98), exceeding human-activity proxies and other driver groups. These results highlight the potential of combining remote sensing with ML to provide a spatially explicit, long-term baseline for DOC monitoring and attribution in large optically complex lakes, thereby improving understanding of lake carbon dynamics under anthropogenic pressures and climate change.

title: Global assessment of extreme precipitation in response to climate warming: revisiting the Clausius–Clapeyron relation
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 676 Author(s): Yishuo Liu, Yuting Yang, Zhuoyi Tu, Yuhan Guo
abstract: The Clausius–Clapeyron (C–C) relationship suggests that rising temperatures under global warming should enhance the atmosphere’s moisture-holding capacity, leading to intensified extreme precipitation (P E) at an expected rate of approximately 7% per degree Celsius. However, observational studies often report deviations from this theoretical expectation. A key methodological distinction lies in whether extremes are defined conditionally within temperature bins or unconditionally from the full precipitation distribution. The conventional binning technique method characterizes the variation of upper-quantile precipitation across temperature bins, but it does not directly capture the intensity changes of true P E over the temperatures where these extremes occur. Here, we introduce a complementary approach that first identifies unconditional true P E from the full precipitation record and then examines how their intensity varies with temperature. Applying this method to global observational data for the past five decades, we find that approximately 85% of regions exhibit positive P E–T scaling, with a global mean rate of ∼ 2%/°C—substantially lower than the theoretical C–C rate. A physical decomposition framework further reveals that non-thermodynamic factors, particularly atmospheric dynamics and precipitation efficiency, play a major role in suppressing the scaling rate, especially in tropical regions. These results suggest that the response of extreme precipitation to warming is more complex than previously assumed, underscoring the importance of incorporating dynamic and microphysical processes into climate projections of hydrological extremes.

title: Parametrization and improvement of the soil evaporation estimation model: Coupling superposition based on fractional canopy cover and soil moisture
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 676 Author(s): Xuefeng Qiu, Xiaoyang Liang, Hang Wang, Jiandong Wang, Guoli Li, Lei Zhang, Hao Zhang, Dingtian Zhou, Xurong Mei
abstract: Estimating soil evaporation (Es) is crucial to accurately regulate the composition of crop water consumption and optimize regional agricultural water use strategies. However, its nonlinear characteristics pose challenges for accurately estimating Es. Focusing on shallow subsurface drip irrigation (SSDI) and surface drip irrigation (DI), this study, within a reference Es modeling framework, pursues two objectives: (i) replace leaf area index (LAI) with fractional canopy cover (fc ) to represent attenuation of surface net radiation (Rns), and (ii) incorporate soil water content (θ) and the surface wetted fraction (P) to develop a unified Es model applicable to both SSDI and DI. Plot-scale experiments show that fc can substitute for LAI in computing the dynamics of Rns; a model using an fc -based parameterization energy term together with a vapor-pressure-deficit (VPD) term achieved R2 = 0.71. With θ and P further included, the unified model yielded R2 = 0.73 and RMSE < 0.33 in validation. We provided an Es model with high prediction accuracy by parameterizing Rns and employing multi-parameter coupling superposition. The key parameters (fc , θ) can be efficiently and rapidly acquired using agricultural informatization techniques, such as drones and sensors. Consequently, this study holds substantial scientific significance and practical value for rapidly and accurately determining regional water-consumption structures and scientifically guiding irrigation water scheduling.

title: Physical ventilation failure drives rapid reservoir hypoxia during heatwaves
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 676 Author(s): Siqian Qiu, Lianghong Long, Hui Xu, Zhongyong Yang, Yufen Ren, Yubo Huang, Daobin Ji
abstract: Climate warming is accelerating deoxygenation in stratified reservoirs, yet distinguishing whether rapid hypoxia stems from enhanced biological consumption or suppressed physical ventilation remains a challenge. This uncertainty hinders effective mitigation during extreme weather events. Here, we combined spatial surveys with high-frequency time series in the Pengxi River (Three Gorges Reservoir) to disentangle these competing mechanisms during a rapid deoxygenation event, where hypoxia covered ∼74% of the water column within 11 days. Quantitative attribution revealed that oxygen-supply reduction dominated the hypoxia (68%–72%), whereas oxygen-demand increase played a secondary role (28%–32%). This physical control was further validated by a tight quantitative coupling, where each unit relaxation in maximum buoyancy frequency (N2_max) drove a ∼3.8 mg/L rebound in bottom-water DO (ΔDO = 3.79 × ΔN2_max − 0.19, R2 = 0.87). Mechanistically, the heatwave imposed a “dual-lock” on bottom water: (i) surface heating intensified the thermocline, effectively shutting down vertical mixing; and (ii) thermal buoyancy altered inflow trajectories, diverting oxygen-rich water from plunging currents to surface interflows, thereby starving the hypolimnion of replenishment. The results explain why intense thermal events trigger rapid deoxygenation and suggest that monitoring physical stability, rather than just water quality, is critical for forecasting. The partitioning approach is transferable to stratified reservoirs, supporting risk-based management under a warming climate.

title: Coupled controls of river stage dynamics and vegetation evapotranspiration on the retention of dissolved organic carbon in the riparian zone
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 676 Author(s): Zhibo Zhang, Shaolin Yang, Chaomeng Dai, Zhi Li
abstract: Riparian zones serve as crucial transitional zones linking terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems. Their intense hydrological exchange processes render them significant hotspots for biogeochemical cycling. However, the combined influence of hydraulic forcing induced by river stage fluctuations and ecological regulation driven by vegetation evapotranspiration on the migration of externally sourced dissolved organic carbon (DOC) remains insufficiently understood. This study developed a coupled numerical model simulating the movement of soil water and solute transport under variable saturation conditions. A vertical two-dimensional simulation domain was established based on China’s Jianghan Plain. Multiple numerical scenarios were designed with different river stage amplitudes ranging from 0 to 1.5 m and leaf area index scaling coefficients ( L A I s c ) ranging from 0 to 1.5. The model systematically analysed the interactive effects governing riparian DOC exchange fluxes, their spatiotemporal distribution, and enrichment processes. The results showed that river stage fluctuations acted as the primary physical driver controlling the strength of external solute inputs. In contrast, vegetation cover primarily reshaped internal solute distribution by altering the hydrodynamic field. The hydraulic pump effect generated by vegetation transpiration, coupled with in situ evaporation and concentration processes, jointly drove the active accumulation of solutes from deep pore water towards the root zone. The temporal analysis revealed a pronounced counterclockwise hysteresis in the response of DOC transport to hydraulic gradients. This pattern indicated that vegetation evapotranspiration effectively retained high solute concentrations during the recession phase of river stage fluctuations. Moreover, the fitted results from the Generalized Additive Model (GAM) indicate that a nonlinear threshold in soil hydraulic properties constrains the enhancing effect of vegetation on solute enrichment. At low cover levels, increased vegetation significantly boosts enrichment efficiency. However, when leaf area index (LAI) exceeds the threshold of 4.5, the partial effect actually shows a declining trend. In summary, this study clarifies the physical mechanisms of solute transport in riparian zones, explaining its shift from hydraulic-driven input to vegetation-controlled retention. These findings provide a scientific basis for managing riparian carbon sinks through optimized vegetation and hydrologic regulation.

title: Groundwater pumping alters land-sourced solute transport in tide-controlled coastal aquifers
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 676 Author(s): Qian Chen, Haixia Shui, Chengji Shen, Jiaxu Zhang, Chunhui Lu
abstract: The increasing proliferation of pumping wells worldwide and the existence of tidal aquifers necessitate a systematic understanding of how groundwater pumping and tides would jointly influence the fate of land-sourced solute in unconfined coastal aquifers. This study numerically addresses the research gap by considering a land-sourced conservative solute plume in a 2-D-cross-shore unconfined coastal aquifer. The results demonstrate that groundwater pumping significantly alters the land-sourced solute transport trajectory and causes the plume sucked into the well, forming a cusp-shaped cone. Meanwhile, pumping greatly modifies the solute dispersion pattern from unimodal to bimodal, reduces the maximum dispersion area and prolongs the residual time of solute plume in the aquifer. Furthermore, pumping concentrates the solute efflux in a narrower zone and shifts the position of maximum solute efflux from the low-tide mark to a lower position. The sensitivity analysis highlights that solute dispersion is strongly influenced by the pumping rate and well location, while the vertical distance between the well and solute source affects significantly solute retention. These findings provide mechanistic insights into complex solute transport in pumped tidal aquifers and support sustainable management of coastal groundwater resources.

title: Analysis of the dependence of daily rainfall depth on wet spell duration across Europe
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 676 Author(s): Carmelo Agnese, Giorgio Baiamonte, Carmelo Cammalleri, Elvira Di Nardo, Stefano Ferraris, Tommaso Martini
abstract: • Dependency between rainfall depth (h) and occurrence (ws) is investigated in Europe. • The Polylog distribution is able to properly model the distribution of h|ws. • A simple logarithmic growth function is proposed to capture this dependency. The statistical modelling of daily rainfall depth is commonly carried out independently from the rainfall occurrence process (dry/wet alternation). In this study, we investigate the effects of accounting for the dependence between rainfall depth ( h ) and wet spell duration ( ws ) using rain gauge data collected on 34 sites across Europe between 1971 and 2016. For each site, a set of conditioned h | ws sub-datasets was generated, and the two-parameter Polylog distribution was fitted on these sub-datasets. The results of the fittings highlight a good capability of the Polylog distribution to capture the statistical behavior of h | ws , as well as the presence of statistically significant differences in the various h | ws fittings obtained in some of the sites. This dependence has been quantified as “Weak” in about 13 sites (38%), and “Strong” in 9 sites (26%). The h | ws dependence was directly modelled for each site with a logarithmic function, showing how this approach is able to well reproduce the arithmetic and geometric means of the sub-samples (standard estimate errors of 0.62 and 0.42 mm, respectively). An attempt at explaining the spatial variability of the dependence through a penalized regression highlighted some key factors, such as longitude and distance from the shoreline; however, the selected features only partially explained the variability and the connection to climate factors. Overall, this research introduces a simple procedure to directly account for the h | ws dependence, which can provide a more robust modelling of the rainfall processes, as well as an improved understanding of the rainfall generating processes

title: Daily inference of reservoir surface water area at large scales via a systematic deep learning framework synergistically integrating multisource remote sensing imagery
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 676 Author(s): Yunye Feng, Lihua Xiong, Qiumei Ma, Shuang Li, Xiongfeng Bai, Mengran Tang
abstract: Reservoir surface water area (SWA) serves as a pivotal indicator for characterizing storage changes and water balance, with important implications for assessing the effects of anthropogenic regulation and protecting aquatic ecosystems. Although satellite observations offer indispensable data support for reservoir SWA monitoring, the trade-off between spatial and temporal resolutions in single-source satellite datasets severely impedes the comprehensive quantification of rapid SWA dynamics. To address this challenge, we develop a systematic deep learning framework for daily SWA inference that synergistically combines cloud-free optical image reconstruction and surface water extraction. The reconstruction module generates daily cloud-free Landsat-like optical images by fusing heterogeneous data from Sentinel-1, MODIS, and Landsat-derived NDVI via a multi-branch feature fusion mechanism. Using the reconstructed imagery as input, the surface water extraction module accurately delineates reservoir SWA. Comparative experiments demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves robust performance in cloud-free image reconstruction (RMSE = 0.021, SSIM = 0.737) and high accuracy in water extraction, with both user’s and producer’s accuracies exceeding 0.970. The framework is applied to 288 large reservoirs across the Yangtze River Basin, and its scalability for large-scale inference is further validated using in situ water elevation measurements from 77 reservoirs. Overall, this framework provides a robust and scalable solution for daily large-scale reservoir SWA inference, laying a solid foundation for hydrological analysis, optimal reservoir operation, and sustainable water resource management.

title: Water levels shape different dissolved organic matter chemistry across Yellow River Deltaic distributary channels
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 676 Author(s): Yuping Zhou, Yuxuan Zhu, Yihua Xiao, Kai Wang, Zhenwei Yan, Ding He, Yujue Wang
abstract: River deltas supply a substantial source of DOM to oceans and exert a disproportionate control on marine biogeochemistry by splitting the fluvial flow into several branches. Although water levels is a critical factor altering biogeochemical processes of DOM, the role of water levels in modulating DOM composition and reactivity across different distributary channels of deltas remains unclear. In this study, two main distributary channels with different water levels of the Yellow River Delta were selected to feature DOM sources and composition by employing mass spectrometry, fluorescence spectroscopy and statistical analysis. Results display that water levels shape different DOM composition in deltaic distributary channels. The primary distributary channel with high water level facilitates the export of fluvial terrestrial DOM throughout deltas, whereas low water level promotes internal cycling of autochthonous phytoplankton-derived organic matter and allochthonous soil organic matter in secondary distributary channels. Internal biogeochemical processes of secondary distributary channels increase the abundance of labile DOM and N/S-containing compounds, and their discharges could alter coastal biogeochemistry through microbial remineralizations. Enriched CRAM could also imply that secondary distributary channels contribute to the refractory carbon pool of coastal oceans. These findings clarify secondary distributary channels with low water levels assert different controls on the export of organic matter throughout river deltas, and numerous secondary distributary channels of river deltas could be the overlooked way transferring diverse DOM from lands to oceans. Linking hydrological conditions of distributary channels with DOM features would be a better way to quantifying the role of river deltas in carbon transfer and has important implications for coastal ecosystems.

title: A flow-direction guided spatiotemporal graph neural network (FD-STGNN) framework for multi-source soil moisture data fusion over the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 676 Author(s): Xinghao Li, Qinli Yang, Junran Yang, Junming Shao
abstract: Accurate soil moisture estimation over the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau (QTP) remains challenging due to complex terrain and climate conditions, and the limited reliability of individual data products. To address this issue, we propose a Flow-Direction Guided Spatiotemporal Graph Neural Network (FD-STGNN) framework for multi-source soil moisture data fusion, integrating in situ observations (ISMN), satellite retrievals (AMSR2), and auxiliary variables. The proposed framework explicitly incorporates terrain-induced flow direction as a physical prior to construct a directed graph, where 0.1° grid cells serve as nodes and hydrological connectivity defines edges. A hybrid architecture combining CNN, LSTM and Graph Attention Network (GAT) is employed to capture spatial features, temporal dynamics, and upstream–downstream dependencies, respectively. Spatial five-fold cross-validation over the QTP shows that compared with the original AMSR2 data, the fused product substantially improves consistency with in situ observations, increasing correlation coefficient (CC) from 0.52 to 0.82, reducing RMSE from 0.128 to 0.063 m3/m3 (a reduction of 51%) and ubRMSE from 0.089 to 0.044 m3/m3. It outperforms the conventional deep learning (CNN-LSTM) and existing GNN-based models (STGCN, GCN-LSTM). In addition, a daily soil moisture dataset at 0.05° resolution is generated for the period 2012–2019, with reduced systematic overestimation across the QTP. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of incorporating flow direction constraints into graph-based frameworks for improving soil moisture estimation in complex terrains.

title: Influences of hydrology and anthropogenic activities on source and quality of dissolved organic matter in karst headwater streams
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 676 Author(s): Shiqin Chen, Y.Jun Xu, Pan Wu, Xingxing Cao, Guangxi Long, Zhangxing Liu
abstract: Dissolved organic matter (DOM) plays an essential role in regulating water quality and biogeochemical processes in aquatic ecosystems. However, how hydrological variability interacts with anthropogenic disturbance to shape DOM dynamics in karst headwater rivers — particularly under wastewater inputs — remains poorly understood. In this study, we investigated the sources and composition of DOM in three headwater streams draining an urban-dominated, an agriculture-dominated, and a forest-dominated catchment, all located in one of the world’s most significant karst regions in Southwest China. Field sampling and measurements were conducted during a dry-cool season and a wet-warm season. Our results reveal that hydrology is the primary driver of DOM source and composition, with runoff and in-stream production dominating during the wet-warm season, and longer water residence time promoting microbial processing during the dry-cool season. Superimposed on these seasonal patterns are clear spatial differences linked to land use/land cover (LULC) types and human activities. The stream draining the agriculture-dominated catchment exhibited a predominance of terrestrial DOM inputs, whereas streams in the urban-dominated and forest-dominated catchments showed evidence of higher microbial activity. Wastewater significantly reshapes DOM composition: treated effluents remove labile protein-like components, while untreated sewage enhances nutrient-driven in-stream production and increases the abundance of humic and terrestrial DOM. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that DOM dynamics in karst headwater streams are jointly regulated by hydrological variability and LULC types, offering new insights into anthropogenic impacts on carbon biogeochemistry in karst aquatic systems.

title: Physics-informed gated transformer for robust flash flood forecasting in data-scarce small catchments via variance-constrained learning
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 676 Author(s): Siqi Wei, Xiekang Wang
abstract: Accurate operational flash flood forecasting in small, data-scarce catchments remains a persistent challenge due to sparse monitoring networks, severe spatial scale mismatches, and highly noisy input data. This study proposes a Physics-Informed Gated Transformer with Variance-Constrained Learning. In contrast to hard-constrained Physics-Informed Neural Networks, this framework utilizes hydrological mechanisms as soft inductive biases. First, it integrates a causally-strict, leakage-free baseflow separation and saturation-excess effective rainfall to physically constrain the solution space. Second, a Gated Residual Network is deployed to dynamically filter high-frequency noise from multi-source inputs. Third, a variance-constrained multi-step loss function is mathematically formulated to explicitly penalize the attenuation of flood peaks. Application in the highly flashy Guanshan River Basin demonstrates that the proposed architecture achieves competitive forecasting accuracy at a 1-hour lead time, effectively mitigating systemic phase-lag and performing favorably against strictly recalibrated baselines including HBV (NSE = −0.044) and standard LSTM (NSE = 0.315). The GRN preserves stable predictive accuracy even under 80% synthetic noise injection. Furthermore, Explainable AI attribution via Gradient SHAP empirically indicates that the network handles spatial scale mismatch by deploying coarse ERA5 data primarily as an antecedent moisture “macro-state proxy”. Finally, zero-shot spatial generalization testing on twelve climatically-matched small forested basins drawn from the CAMELS-US dataset shows that the proposed architecture maintains performance comparable to two state-of-the-art large-sample benchmarks and significantly outperforms a Vanilla Transformer counterpart. These findings highlight that coupling soft physical inductive biases with gated architectures offers a transferable, physics-constrained framework for operational early warning in poorly gauged catchments.

title: Enhanced water level fluctuations reduced the competitive advantage of cyanobacteria
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 676 Author(s): Yan Chen, Rui Xia, Ruining Jia, Junde Ming, Kai Zhang, Jinghui Dou, Tianxiang Zhao, Xiang Li, Qin Zhang, Qi Zhang
abstract: Hydrological changes in large river confluence zones, such as the Han River confluence area, driven by water infrastructure and natural inflows, alter regional biogeochemical processes. However, quantitative thresholds of hydrodynamic regimes and their drivers for algal succession remain unclear. This study, focusing on the Yangtze–Han River confluence under the SNWD middle route, refined the classification of flow patterns and developed a method to assess algal competitive advantage. We quantitatively revealed the succession mechanisms of algae under varying flow conditions. Results show: (1) five typical flow patterns were identified: strong and weak flow backward, top support, weak and strong natural flow; (2) the cyanobacterial competitive advantage exhibited a significant three–stage nonlinear response to flow patterns (R2 = 0.682); (3) structural equation modeling revealed three key driving pathways through which flow patterns influence algal succession: hydrodynamic, water temperature, and nutrient pathways. Enhancing hydrodynamic conditions can weaken cyanobacterial competitiveness, thereby mitigating riverine harmful algal bloom risk.

title: Paleo-hydrological controls on continental-shelf groundwater salinity distribution offshore New Jersey, USA
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 676 Author(s): Chong Sheng, Christian Hensen, Ariel T. Thomas, Thomas Müller, Mark Schmidt
abstract: Continental shelves host extensive offshore relatively fresh groundwater (ORFG) systems whose origin, distribution, and persistence are strongly influenced by paleo sea-level fluctuations; however, the paleo-hydrological controls governing their present-day salinity patterns remain poorly constrained. Here, we investigate the ORFG system offshore New Jersey, USA, by integrating high-resolution seismic profiles, borehole constraints, geochemical and isotopic data, and three-dimensional variable-density groundwater flow and solute transport modeling. Model results indicate that most ORFG was emplaced by topographically driven groundwater flow during sea-level lowstands over the past ∼ 100 kyr. During Pleistocene lowstands, enhanced hydraulic gradients across the exposed continental shelf promoted widespread seaward groundwater flow, leading to the development of low-salinity groundwater over large areas. Subsequent marine transgression led to partial salinization through diffusive and density-driven mixing with seawater. Our results further demonstrate that cyclical flushing and re-salinification of shelf sediments over glacial–interglacial timescales are inherently asymmetric, favoring the long-term retention of freshened groundwater. Compared with conventional layered modeling approaches, the incorporation of depth-migrated seismic stratigraphy and geostatistical property modeling substantially improves the characterization of ORFG spatial heterogeneity and volume distribution. However, these results are based on a single representative geostatistical realization and therefore do not explicitly quantify stochastic uncertainty. Overall, this study highlights the long-term legacy of paleo-hydrological conditions on continental-shelf groundwater systems and provides a process-based perspective for interpreting ORFG occurrence, evolution, and vulnerability along passive continental margins.

title: Regulation of river water temperature and dissolved oxygen under cascade reservoir systems: Hydropower-ecological synergy based on a simulation–optimization-causal explanation framework
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 676 Author(s): Zhaoyang Zhu, Zhaocai Wang, Jiachen Kong, Jiahao Zou, Xuanxuan Wang, Zuowen Tan, Chenye Liu, Qikai Liu
abstract: Under the combined pressures of global warming and large-scale cascade damming, river water quality dynamics are increasingly deviating from their natural patterns, resulting in abnormal water temperature (WT) regimes and amplified dissolved oxygen (DO) fluctuations that threaten key ecological processes such as fish spawning. Mitigating the adverse impacts of cascade reservoir operations on downstream ecosystems while ensuring reliable power supply has become a critical challenge for river basin management. To address this issue, this study proposes a multi-objective management framework for cascade reservoirs, termed Simulation–Optimization–Causal Explanation (SOCE). An RF–AdaBoost surrogate model incorporating prior physical knowledge is first developed to simulate WT and DO dynamics under limited water quality observations. The surrogate model is then coupled with a reservoir operation model, and a reinforcement learning (RL)-based NSGA-III algorithm is employed to solve the multi-objective optimization problem balancing hydropower generation and ecological requirements. Furthermore, interpretability is integrated with Convergent Cross-Mapping (CCM) to identify and validate the causal effects of operational decisions on downstream water quality. Using the Xiluodu–Xiangjiaba (XLD-XJB) cascade system as a case study, the results show that hydropower generation increases by 94–106 million kWh, while DO suitability reaches 98.17% under three typical inflow scenarios. The proposed framework effectively enhances total power generation while mitigating ecological risks during fish spawning periods. In addition, its causal interpretability expands the feasible space of ecological scheduling strategies. Overall, the SOCE framework provides a scalable and interpretable decision-support tool for ecological reservoir operation.

title: From subordinate recharge to dominant pollution: the role of lacustrine groundwater discharge in sandy saline-salt lakes
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 676 Author(s): Xiangwei Li, Ruihong Yu, Renpu Wang, Dongchao Huo, Zongbao Yue, Xiaozhuang Wang, Bowen Ye, Ao Gao, Hanyu Li, Yufei Bai, Yuanzhen Zhao, Heyang Sun, Shen Qu, Tingxi Liu, Xixi Lu
abstract: Sandy lakes are ecologically vulnerable to anthropogenic and climatic stressors. Although lacustrine groundwater discharge (LGD) is recognized as a crucial component of lake hydrology and nutrient cycling, its specific role in regulating environmental vulnerability in these sensitive ecosystems remains poorly quantified. This study employed an integrated approach, combining hydrochemical analysis, water source identification, and a radon (222Rn) isotope mass balance model, to investigate the sources and drivers of major pollutants in saline-salt lakes of the Mu Us Sandy Land. Particular emphasis was placed on the impact of LGD on lake water (LW) quality. The enrichment of nitrogen substances and Mg2+ represented the primary environmental issue within the watershed. Total nitrogen (TN), primarily derived from manure application, and total phosphorus (TP), originating from industrial activities, were identified as the major pollutants of groundwater (GW) and LW. Spatially, saline lakes exhibited better water quality than salt lakes, and lakes in the upper and middle reaches generally had better quality than those downstream. Temporally, water quality variations were closely linked to changes in lake surface area, which were predominantly controlled by precipitation-the primary source of lake recharge, accounting for 65.6% of total inflow. The concentration of 222Rn decreased progressively from GW to porewater and then to LW (2030.17, 1477.41, and 40.61 Bq/m3, respectively), indicating active LGD processes, with a mean LGD rate of 63.60 mm/d within the watershed. This process delivered fluxes of 1.88, 7.92, and 3.18 g/m2/d for TN, NO3 –, and Mg2+, respectively, facilitating their accumulation in the lakes. The ratio of GW input height to lake depth revealed that shallower lakes received a greater proportion of water and nutrient inputs via LGD and consequently exhibited poorer water quality, highlighting the substantial regulatory role of LGD on lake environments. Random forest analysis further indicated that mitigation strategies should target the root causes, namely, industrial/agricultural pollution sources and the LGD pathway. Controlling inputs from these terrestrial sources is therefore essential to reduce pollutant loading in GW and limit their influx into lakes.

title: Changes in sediment transport capacity in the lower Yellow River: Analysis using an improved formula based on energy theory
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 676 Author(s): Dong Liang, Zhe Huang, Junzheng Liu, Yan Li, Yuchuan Bai, Haijue Xu
abstract: Sediment transport capacity (STC) is fundamental for quantifying hydro-sediment dynamics in the lower Yellow River (LYR). Since the Xiaolangdi (XLD) reservoir began operating in 2000, downstream flow-sediment conditions in the LYR have changed markedly, with more frequent low-sediment flows, channel adjustment, and riverbed coarsening, rendering traditional STC formulations less suitable for post-XLD conditions. In this study, a new STC formula for the post-XLD LYR was developed within the classical energy-based framework, based on the energy conservation equations of sediment-laden flow. Using a near-equilibrium sediment-transport criterion, 360 sets of measured flow-sediment data from 2000 to 2010 were retained for parameter calibration, and 208 sets of measured data from 2011 to 2022 were used for validation. Comparative evaluation shows that the proposed formula provides the best overall predictive performance for the datasets considered in this study and performs well under post-XLD low-to-moderate sediment concentration conditions. The formula was subsequently applied to investigate the relationships among STC, flow rate, cross-sectional morphology, and bed-material gradation. Results indicate a significant decline in STC after XLD operation, which is interpreted as the result of coupled hydrodynamic, morphological, and bed-material adjustments, with riverbed coarsening acting as one important contributing factor. The proposed formula is intended primarily for similar conditions of post-XLD in LYR, while its application to other alluvial rivers should be understood as restrictive and requires further validation.

title: Precise waterbody mapping at the city scale using a novel connectivity preservation and boundary refinement network based on medium-resolution remote sensing imagery
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 676 Author(s): Han Zhai, Ziyu Liu, Yiran Kuang, Yiming Xiao
abstract: Waterbody mapping has always been a research hotspot, with utmost significance in water resource management. Although deep learning approaches have achieved remarkable accomplishments, most of them are designed for high-resolution images, with limited adaptability to the city scale, and suffered from serious misjudgments, frequent breakages, and rough morphologies in complex scenarios. To overcome these obstacles, this paper proposes an innovative connectivity preservation and boundary refinement network (CB-Net), to precisely delineate waterbodies at the city scale using medium-resolution remote sensing images, which explicitly focuses on geometrical characteristic mining of waterbodies. Specifically, with regard to frequent breakages and rough morphologies, an effective dense dynamic snake convolution module is developed, to deeply learn felicitous geometrical features for various waterbodies and aggregate hierarchical expressions to preserve connectivity, which enables continuous and detailed waterbody extraction. In addition, to improve boundary localization and morphology expressivity, a valid high-frequency multiscale feature fusion module is designed as skip connections, to learn multidirectional high-frequency information and leverage multiscale directional expressions to generate structure-and-position-aware features, thus facilitating fine-grained segmentations. A challenging waterbody dataset based on Sentinel-2 images (S2-Water) is constructed for performance validation, which compensates for the scarcity of specialized datasets and advances future researches. Extensive experimental results illustrate that CB-Net significantly outperformed the other state-of-the-art alternatives to yield promising results for Wuhan City and Jinan City, indicating its good adaptability and generalizability to various waterbodies in complex scenarios. Generally, CB-Net achieved a mean F1-sore of 88.69% and IoU (Intersection over union) of 79.79%, which well satisfies applicational requirements.

title: Mathematical modeling for interactions and transport of particulate bioavailable phosphorus with sediment dynamics
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 676 Author(s): Ya Zhou, Lei Huang, Man Zhang, Danny Reible, Hongwei Fang
abstract: Particulate bioavailable phosphorus (PBAP) plays a critical role in biogeochemical cycling and primary productivity in aquatic ecosystems, particularly in ecologically vulnerable alpine regions. However, the understanding of PBAP dynamics remains limited due to the complex interaction and transport processes. To address this gap, we developed a mathematical model that coupled hydrodynamics, sediment transport, and dissolved and particulate phosphorus dynamics to simulate PBAP transport. PBAP bound to sediment was represented by coupling sediment mineral properties and environmental factors. Lateral inputs of water, sediment, and phosphorus from the watershed were incorporated using the Soil and Water Assessment Tool (SWAT). The model was applied to the Yarlung Tsangpo River and successfully reproduced PBAP distributions, with spatiotemporal concentrations ranging from 0.20 to 0.38 mg g−1, consistent with field measurements. The estimated annual PBAP flux was 2.77 Gg yr−1, partitioned as 46.0% Ex‑P, 37.7% Fe‑P, and 16.3% Al‑P, which exceeded the flux of dissolved phosphorus (∼0.80 Gg yr−1). Furthermore, over 95% of annual PBAP flux occurred between June and September, indicating strong temporal variability in PBAP dynamics within monsoonal alpine basins. This model advances process-based quantifications of PBAP dynamics and has far-reaching implications for water environment management.

title: Crop spatial concentration enhances water productivity while threatening regional agricultural water sustainability
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 676 Author(s): Hongrong Huang, Qiangqiang Rong, Yiping Wu, Yulei Xie, Wei Wang, Xiangxiang Ji, Zenghui Xu, Jie Gao, Meirong Su, La Zhuo
abstract: Crop production is increasingly concentrated in fewer regions, but whether this spatial concentration improves water productivity at the expense of regional agricultural water sustainability remains unclear. Here, we investigate this efficiency–sustainability trade-off for rice, wheat, and maize production in China from 2000 to 2021. We integrated AquaCrop simulations with water footprint accounting, a production concentration index, planetary-boundary-based sustainability assessment, and panel quantile regression to quantify crop concentration and its heterogeneous effects on water productivity and regional agricultural water sustainability. Results showed that the spatial concentration indices of rice, wheat, and maize increased by 8.0%, 17.6% and 9.8%, respectively, between 2000 and 2021. Increasing crop concentration improved water productivity but reduced regional agricultural water sustainability, revealing a clear trade-off.
