This study, conducted under real aquaculture conditions in a radioactively contaminated area, demonstrated that adding the veterinary drug Ferrocyn 2 to feed is an effective and inexpensive countermeasure for reducing the activity concentration of radiocesium in the body of carp fish.

title: Natural radioactivity and GIS mapping of soils in Binh Phuoc, Vietnam
description: Publication date: May 2026 Source: Journal of Environmental Radioactivity, Volume 296 Author(s): Thuy Duong Tran, Ngoc Ha Bui, Dinh Thuy Mai, Tien Hung Bui, Tat Thang Nguyen, Hai Quan Ho
abstract: This study investigates the natural radioactivity in 500 soil samples collected across Binh Phuoc Province, Vietnam, a region characterized by basalt formations and bauxite mining. Activity concentrations of 226Ra, 232Th, 40K, and 137Cs were measured using gamma spectrometry, with spatial distributions mapped at a 1:60,000 scale using a QGIS software. Results revealed 226Ra ranging from 5.88 to 63.17 Bq.kg−1, 232Th from 17.78 to 117.33 Bq.kg−1, 40K from 111.42 to 1019.90 Bq/kg, and negligible 137Cs of about 0.26 Bq.kg−1. Radiological hazard indices, including radium equivalent activity (Raeq: 117.42 Bq.kg−1) and external hazard index (Hex: 0.317), remained below international thresholds of 370 Bq.kg−1 and 1, respectively, indicating low environmental risk. Driven by a high sampling density (approximately 1 sample per 14 km2), the detailed geographic information systems (GIS) maps provide the first high-resolution baseline for naturally occurring radioactive materials (NORM) monitoring and support bauxite mining management as well as agricultural safety assessments in southeastern Vietnam. This research contributes significant data to the limited literature on natural radioactivity in Southeast Asian soils.

title: Radiocarbon activity of gases in urban surface air in Bratislava, Slovakia
description: Publication date: May 2026 Source: Journal of Environmental Radioactivity, Volume 296 Author(s): I. Kontul, P.P. Povinec, M. Richtáriková, A. Cherkinsky, J. Šimon, M. Ješkovský, J. Kaizer
abstract: Carbon-containing gases in the atmosphere are important for the study of carbon cycle dynamics and anthropogenic influence on these environmental processes. Radiocarbon analysis is an excellent tool for studying sources of these gases and their variations. Carbon dioxide is the most abundant and most important of these gases and this study presents results of radiocarbon measurements of carbon dioxide samples collected at the campus of Comenius University in Bratislava, Slovakia from 1967 to 2025. This record of radiocarbon activity is characterized by decreasing intensity of anthropogenic effects in last 30 years. Local Suess effect (dilution of radiocarbon activity by radiocarbon-free fossil carbon dioxide) is clearly weaker in recent decades. The influence of Slovak nuclear power plants (input of excess anthropogenic radiocarbon) is also significantly smaller in last decades compared to the beginning of radiocarbon activity record from Bratislava. Comparison of two sampling stations located in Bratislava with clean air data showed that there is significant contrast between local Suess effect intensity observed at locations relatively close to each other within the city, but in a different setting in terms of local fossil carbon dioxide sources. Radiocarbon analysis of carbon dioxide in Bratislava has also been recently supplemented by sampling and analysis of carbon monoxide and hydrocarbons present in the atmosphere. The results show that their radiocarbon levels are considerably influenced by their fossil sources, leading to their very low radiocarbon activity compared to expected background values.

title: A georeferenced baseline and GIS-based screening of natural radioactivity in coastal sediments and nearshore waters of Da Nang, Viet Nam
description: Publication date: May 2026 Source: Journal of Environmental Radioactivity, Volume 296 Author(s): Hoang Thanh-Phi Hung, Cao Van Chung, Nguyen Van An, Le Ngoc Vuong, Duong Van Thang
abstract: This study establishes a georeferenced 2023 baseline of natural radioactivity in coastal sediments, nearshore seawater, and adjacent surface soils of Da Nang City, Viet Nam, and evaluates its utility for screening-level interpretation of coastal environmental processes. A total of 36 samples were analysed, comprising 15 coastal sediments, 15 paired nearshore seawater samples, and 6 surface soils. Activity concentrations of 226Ra, 232Th-series radionuclides (represented by 228Ac), and 40K were determined by high-resolution HPGe gamma-ray spectrometry. Radiological assessment was restricted to pathway-consistent outdoor exposure metrics for solid matrices, including absorbed dose rate in air (Dout), outdoor annual effective dose (AEDEout), and external hazard index (Hex). In coastal sediments, Dout ranged from 58.9 to 90.2 nGy h−1 (mean: 70.8 nGy h−1), corresponding to AEDEout values of 0.072-0.111 mSv y−1, while Hex remained below unity at all sites, indicating low external radiological concern. Surface soils showed comparatively higher, yet still moderate, natural radioactivity levels, whereas nearshore seawater was characterised by the expected predominance of dissolved 40K and substantially lower 226Ra and 228Ac activities consistent with background coastal marine conditions. Beyond baseline characterisation, inter-radionuclide relationships and spatial variation in the 226Ra/228Ac activity ratio revealed heterogeneity consistent with lithogenic control, sediment compositional variability, and possible hydrodynamic sorting effects. GIS-based interpolation further delineated coherent alongshore gradients rather than isolated anomalies, supporting a process-consistent interpretation of radionuclide distributions at the screening level. The study therefore provides both a defensible environmental radioactivity baseline for the Da Nang coastal zone and a reproducible framework for spatially explicit radiological screening and long-term coastal monitoring.

title: Tracing submarine groundwater discharge in a semi-enclosed bay using pulsed ionization chamber radon detector
description: Publication date: May 2026 Source: Journal of Environmental Radioactivity, Volume 296 Author(s): Chunqian Li, Shibin Zhao, Lu Cao, Yue Pang, Lijun Song, Xiaopeng Lv, Bochao Xu
abstract: Natural occurring radon (222Rn, t 1/2 = 3.8 d) is a powerful tracer for investigating submarine groundwater discharge (SGD) and other hydrological and oceanographic processes. Continuous 222Rn measurement approach is essential but remains inadequate to provide high spatiotemporal resolution field dataset, especially for low-activity surface seawaters. Here, we present a labor-less technique for continuous 222Rn observations using the pulsed ionization chamber detector (PIC-1000). The measurement efficiency of PIC-1000 is ∼7 and ∼3.5 times that of the commercial RAD7 and the existing PIC-200 detectors, respectively. High efficiency and low background make the PIC-1000 device more suitable for low and variable radon activity measuring environments. Based on over 18-day continuous field measurements and a radon mass balance model, we estimated the groundwater flux at 12.6 ± 8.9 cm d−1 in a semi-enclosed bay during wet season of 2023. We further identified a positive correlation between groundwater flow and tidal amplitude within individual tidal cycles, highlighting the dynamic response of groundwater-seawater interactions to both diurnal flooding-ebbing and biweekly spring-neap tidal forcing.

title: Physics-informed deep learning for rapid marine radionuclide dispersion forecasting in nuclear emergency response
description: Publication date: May 2026 Source: Journal of Environmental Radioactivity, Volume 296 Author(s): Zhiqiang Cui, Xiong Wu, Yonghong Liu, Zhihong Liu
abstract: In the event of a severe nuclear accident at a coastal nuclear power plant, the rapid and accurate assessment of radionuclide dispersion in surrounding coastal waters is critical for effective emergency response. To overcome the inherent latency and predictive fidelity limitations of conventional marine dispersion simulations, this study develops an innovative hybrid Physics-Informed Deep Learning (PIDL) framework. The framework integrates an optimized Joseph's instantaneous point source model, which provides a rapid baseline prediction incorporating radionuclide decay and atmospheric deposition, with a Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model (DDPM). The DDPM is uniquely employed to learn the complex distribution of the physical model's residual error, effectively reconstructing a high-fidelity concentration field from a biased initial prediction. To comprehensively validate the model's performance and generalization capabilities, we utilized two distinct and representative radionuclide release scenarios: the acute, high-concentration release from the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant (FDNPP) accident and the chronic, low-level discharges into the Irish Sea from the Sellafield facility. The results demonstrate that the PIDL model significantly outperforms the standalone physical model. On the Fukushima dataset, the coefficient of determination ( R 2 ) for 137Cs concentration prediction improved from 0.78 (physics-only) to 0.96 (hybrid model), with a corresponding 68% reduction in the Root Mean Square Error (RMSE). Critically, predictions are generated within seconds, meeting the stringent time constraints of emergency response. Furthermore, this study establishes a clear framework linking the model's rapid predictions to the principles of Probabilistic Safety Assessment (PSA) and specific nuclear emergency response actions. The model's outputs provide dynamic, data-driven inputs for consequence analysis, supporting dynamic hazard zone mapping, optimization of monitoring resources, and public communication strategies. This work presents a computationally efficient tool designed to support decision-making in the critical early stages of a coastal nuclear emergency.

title: Monte Carlo simulation-based characteristics of indoor radon concentrations and exploratory probabilistic risk analysis in university buildings
description: Publication date: May 2026 Source: Journal of Environmental Radioactivity, Volume 296 Author(s): Yuefei Ma, Mingya Wang, Decheng Qin, Xuechun Zhang, Chunhui Zhang, Qiao Han, Fengcheng Jiang, Mingfei Xing, Xiaoming Guo, Chuanbing Zhang, Pinghua Huang, Mingshi Wang
abstract: This study systematically investigated the indoor radon concentration levels and their seasonal distribution characteristics in typical functional spaces at a university in Jiaozuo, China. This study exploratorily used the instantaneous electrostatic collection method to measure the air radon concentration at specific moments in various buildings for dose analysis, revealed the illusion of 'average safety' in traditional deterministic approaches. The results showed that spatially, student dormitory exhibited the highest annual average concentration (47 Bq·m−3), while laboratory building had the lowest (27 Bq·m−3). Temporally, radon concentrations followed a distinct seasonal pattern of winter > autumn > spring > summer. Temperature was identified as a key environmental factor influencing radon levels, showing a significant negative correlation with radon concentration overall. Although the average risk in all regions is lower than the acceptable level, there is a 5% chance that student dormitory will reach 2.4 times of the low-risk scenario (5% quantile). As an exploratory application, this study provides methodological insights for identifying high-risk populations and formulating targeted management strategies.

title: Impact of wildfire on the distribution and migration of plutonium and cesium isotopes in forest soils, Lu mountain, Sichuan
description: Publication date: May 2026 Source: Journal of Environmental Radioactivity, Volume 296 Author(s): Yongjing Guan, Guodong Yu, Mengmeng Wu, Xianghao Luo, Wenjian Huang, Yukun Li, Zhiyi Tu, Chunping Huang, Jianhui Lai, Deyu Wang, Zhanhong Guo, Huijuan Wang, Zhiyong Liu
abstract: To investigate the distribution and migration of radionuclides in forest soils following fire disturbance, this study selected Lu Mountain in Xichang City, Sichuan Province, as the study area, and measured the activity concentrations and vertical distribution patterns of 137Cs and 239+240Pu. Results show that the activity concentrations of 239+240Pu in surface soils ranged from 0.11 ± 0.01 to 0.85 ± 0.03 Bq/kg, while those of 137Cs ranged from 2.84 ± 0.18 to 16.20 ± 0.80 Bq/kg. The total inventories of 239+240Pu and 137Cs in the soil profiles were 84-194 Bq/m2 and 3123-10910 Bq/m2, respectively. Both 137Cs and 239+240Pu exhibited bimodal vertical distributions, with notable surface enrichment, suggesting that fire disturbance altered soil structure and promoted short-term migration and local accumulation of these radionuclides. To quantify the migration of 239+240Pu, the convection-dispersion equation (CDE) was applied to simulate and predict its behavior. Additionally, fire simulation experiments were conducted to further examine the impact of wildfires on radionuclide migration. The results indicate that fire caused a minor loss of Cs+ from the soil. However, due to the short experimental duration, no significant difference in the Cs+ migration rate was observed.

title: Spatiotemporal changes in 137 Cs concentration in Japanese flounder Paralichthys olivaceus in Sendai Bay and the adjacent area off the coast of Fukushima Prefecture in relation to the dynamic states of 137 Cs in the ecosystem
description: Publication date: May 2026 Source: Journal of Environmental Radioactivity, Volume 296 Author(s): Yutaka Kurita, Yuya Shigenobu, Hiroyuki Togashi, Takami Morita, Shinta Sakurai, Hideki Kaeriyama
abstract: This study aimed to assess the spatiotemporal changes in 137Cs concentrations in Japanese flounder Paralichthys olivaceus in water around the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Station (FDNPS) following the accident that occurred in March 2011 and to clarify the dynamic state of the nuclide in the ecosystem. In Sendai Bay (approximately 50–100 km north of the FDNPS) and off the coast of Fukushima Prefecture, we examined changes in 137Cs concentrations in seawater near the seabed and Japanese flounder during 2011–2022, and in the main prey species during 2015–2022. The 137Cs concentrations in the bottom seawater were classified into seven clusters: the deeper the water and the farther the location from the FDNPS, the lower the concentration. The 137Cs concentrations in Japanese flounder (standardized to 500 mm total length [TL]) in Sendai Bay were generally in the following order: 2007–2009 year classes (YCs) > 2010 YC > 2011–2020 YCs. In addition, 137Cs concentrations in Japanese flounder in Sendai Bay were lower than those off the coast of Fukushima Prefecture. 137Cs concentrations in seawater and Japanese flounder have been decreasing; however, the rate of decline has slowed in recent years. The 137Cs concentration ratio of Japanese flounder to seawater in 2021 was approximately 220, which was higher than the value at the equilibrium state (78) derived from stable Cs and higher than their main prey species (33–59) even considering biomagnification, and has been decreasing only very slowly over the past several years. In addition to these results, the 137Cs–TL relationship and other characteristics, compared with those of stable Cs, indicate that the 137Cs concentration in Japanese flounder for the 2011–2020 YCs from 2016 to 2022 was in a transient or quasi-equilibrium state with a high concentration ratio and a slight decrease.

title: Characterizing mud volcanic activity through terrestrial gamma radiation: Insights into subsurface processes at the Piparo Mud Volcano, Trinidad and Tobago
description: Publication date: May 2026 Source: Journal of Environmental Radioactivity, Volume 296 Author(s): K.T. Ramjarrie, K.S. Banerjee, D. Davis, L. Sobers, O.O. Blake
abstract: The Piparo Mud Volcano is a significant natural hazard in Trinidad and Tobago, highlighted by its violent 1997 eruption and subsequent heightened activity in 2019, 2024, and 2025. These events arise from overpressurized subsurface conditions that force fluidized mud and gas to the surface. Despite these ongoing risks, current monitoring frameworks remain surface-based and event-driven, offering limited insight into deeper structural and geophysical precursors of activity. To address this gap, this study applies gamma radiation monitoring to: (1) explore correlations between spatial radiation patterns and geomorphological features, (2) examine temporal variations, and (3) evaluate its potential to predict volcanic activity. Measurements were collected at 40 locations over a 29-month period at six intervals (0, 4, 11, 17, 23, 29), using a Geiger-Müller counter, positioned 1 m above ground level (GL) and 0.5 m below GL. The results revealed contrasting spatial patterns above and below GL, with elevated surface gamma radiation in fracture-dense southern and eastern crater areas, while below GL radiation peaked in opposing pressurized zones. Gamma radiation also varied systematically across three distinct phases: pre-activity (months 0-11), active (months 11-17), and post-activity (months 17-29). During pre-activity, gamma radiation increased above GL and declined below GL, then converged prior to an expulsion event in month 13, and diverged again during post-activity. These patterns demonstrate a clear link between gamma radiation fluctuations and mud volcanic activity, highlighting a novel method for early detection and improved hazard assessment.

title: Updated ICRP dosimetry amplifies limitations of WHO adult-based radium screening: implications for early-life and lifetime exposure
description: Publication date: May 2026 Source: Journal of Environmental Radioactivity, Volume 296 Author(s): Alaaddin Alnajjar, Majd Hawwari
abstract: Chronic ingestion of naturally occurring radionuclides in drinking water remains a significant source of long-term population exposure. The World Health Organization (WHO) radiological screening framework is derived from adult ingestion assumptions and adult dose coefficients adopted from legacy ICRP publications (ICRP 72/119), thereby masking age-specific vulnerabilities in early life. ICRP Publication 158 introduces updated adult ingestion dose coefficients based on revised computational phantoms and internal dosimetry models. This study evaluates the regulatory implications of substituting ICRP 158 adult coefficients into the existing adult-based WHO screening framework. Radium-228 and radium-226 were analyzed using age-dependent lifetime dose modeling from birth to 70 years. The results reveal a fundamental dosimetric paradox: although ICRP 158 reduces adult ingestion dose estimates by approximately 50%, these reductions are not proportionally reflected in the age groups that dominate peak exposure. For Ra-228, the dominant exposure window shifts to age one, driven by infant intake patterns, reaching an annual dose nearly 12 times higher than the updated adult screening proxy. For Ra-226, the divergence between the declining adult baseline and the comparatively unchanged early-life peak substantially widens. These findings demonstrate that strict adherence to adult-based screening under the updated coefficient framework creates a regulatory blind spot, where formal compliance may obscure disproportionate early-life dose burdens. To address this structural limitation, lifetime (Flife, representing the lifetime-averaged annual effective dose per unit concentration) and peak (Fpeak, representing the maximum age-specific annual effective dose per unit concentration) screening factors are proposed as practical, guideline-compatible enhancements that restore protective intent without compromising operational simplicity.

title: Survey of radon concentrations and dose estimation in 87 greenhouses in China
description: Publication date: May 2026 Source: Journal of Environmental Radioactivity, Volume 296 Author(s): Jialu Li, Yunyun Wu, Yanchao Song, Yinping Su, Haoran Sun, Bowei Ding, Changsong Hou
abstract: Radon (222Rn) is a major natural radiation source and the second leading cause of lung cancer after smoking. Greenhouses, as semi-enclosed environments, may accumulate elevated levels of radon, potentially increasing lung cancer risk among workers. Radon concentrations were measured in 90 greenhouses across 28 cities in China using CR-39 detectors, with exposure durations mainly for three months, and in a few cases, for one or two months. Information on greenhouse type, ventilation type, and irrigation water sources was also collected. A total of 416 measurements from 87 greenhouses were obtained. The results showed an arithmetic mean radon concentration of 166 Bq/m3, a geometric mean of 106 Bq/m3, and a range of 11–2326 Bq/m3. 12% of the measurements exceeded 300 Bq/m3, and 1% exceeded 1000 Bq/m3. Factors such as regional differences, greenhouse type, ventilation type and irrigation water source influence radon concentrations in greenhouses. The mean annual effective dose for greenhouse workers was 1.46 mSv, with a range of 0.1–20.4 mSv. The findings of this study indicate substantial regional variations in radon levels in greenhouses across China. Attention should be paid to greenhouses with elevated radon concentrations and to the health of workers. Improving ventilation efficiency and optimizing greenhouse design can reduce radon accumulation.

title: Radiocesium uptake and distribution in Japanese cedar ( Cryptomeria japonica D. Don): A review of current knowledge and future perspectives
description: Publication date: May 2026 Source: Journal of Environmental Radioactivity, Volume 296 Author(s): Muyiwa Michael Orosun, Vasyl Yoschenko, Kenji Nanba
abstract: The Fukushima Dai-ichi Nuclear Power Plant accident in March 2011 released large quantities of radiocesium (137Cs) into the environment, contaminating vast forested areas. The forest account for nearly 70% of Fukushima Prefecture. With a half-life of 30.2 years, 137Cs remains the dominant source of long-term radiological concern in forest ecosystems, where it can contribute to human and wildlife exposure through external irradiation, food chain transfer, and secondary environmental releases. Among affected species, Japanese cedar (Cryptomeria japonica), the most dominant conifer in Japan, has been a focal point of research due to its ecological importance and economic value for timber production. Recent studies have revealed unexpected and species-specific patterns of 137Cs distribution in cedar stems. Although initial contamination was dominated by sapwood enrichment immediately after fallout, subsequent monitoring showed progressive translocation into heartwood, leading to heartwood/sapwood concentration ratios exceeding 2–3 by 2020. This anomalous enrichment, linked to heartwood moisture and potassium content, contrasts sharply with Konara oak and Japanese red pine, which remain sapwood-dominated, and cypress and larch, which tend toward equilibrium. Such findings highlight complex transport mechanisms involving xylem and phloem pathways, ray parenchyma activity, and diffusion processes, as well as strong influences of environmental and site-specific factors. Understanding these dynamics is essential for predicting the long-term fate of 137Cs in forest ecosystems, managing radiological risks, and guiding forestry practices, including safe timber utilization and effective remediation strategies. This review synthesizes current knowledge on radial and vertical 137Cs distribution in Japanese cedar stems, explores mechanistic explanations, and highlights key research priorities, including long-term monitoring of heartwood–sapwood redistribution, improved understanding of cesium transport mechanisms, and the development of predictive models to support sustainable forest management in radiologically contaminated landscapes.

title: Developments of analytical techniques for the determination of 237 Np/ 239 Pu atom ratios on air filters from Vienna, Austria
description: Publication date: May 2026 Source: Journal of Environmental Radioactivity, Volume 296 Author(s): Gabriele Wallner, Philipp Rohrbach, Leo J. Krammer, Andreas Wiederin, Peter Steier, Karin Hain
abstract: Air filter samples collected in the 1960s and therefore representing pure weapons test fallout were investigated with respect to 237Np and 239Pu concentrations as well as 237Np/239Pu atom ratios. 237Np and the Pu isotopes (with 242Pu as tracer for both elements) were jointly separated from the matrix using UTEVA resin and were then measured by accelerator mass spectrometry (AMS). Results were normalized to external standards to consider different Np and Pu outputs during the measurement. The resulting 237Np/239Pu atom ratios were slightly higher than the 237Np/239Pu ratios of soil samples from literature. As the radiochemical yields of Np as well as of Pu, investigated by α-spectrometry of samples with added 237Np and 236Pu tracers, indicated chemical fractionation, the filter samples were for comparison also normalized to IAEA-385 reference samples which had been processed collaterally. When using the revised literature value for the 237Np/239Pu ratio of IAEA-385, accordance with the results obtained by normalization to the external standards was found.

title: Analytical approach for 226 Ra, 228 Ra and 210 Pb measurements for environmental monitoring using liquid scintillation spectrometry
description: Publication date: May 2026 Source: Journal of Environmental Radioactivity, Volume 296 Author(s): Hector Hugo Silva Medrado, Verônica Alves dos Santos, Joel Augusto Moura Porto, Rubens Martins Moreira, Carlos Alberto de Carvalho Filho
abstract: Uranium and thorium mining and milling facilities are required to monitor naturally occurring radionuclides (like natU, 226Ra, 228Ra and 210Pb) as part of their Environmental Radiological Monitoring Programs (ERMP), both under routine conditions and during discharge of radioactive effluents or emergency situations. In this work, a rapid and robust analytical method was developed for the determination of 226Ra, 228Ra, and 210Pb in various environmental matrices using liquid scintillation spectrometry. The methodology was specifically designed and validated in accordance with the ERMP requirements of the Uranium Concentration Unit (URA) operated by Brazilian Nuclear Industries (INB). Key performance parameters including chemical recovery, detection limits, counting efficiency, and analytical turnaround time were thoroughly evaluated. Radiochemical separations of radium and lead achieved average chemical yields of approximately 87%, while counting efficiencies reached 90% for 226Ra, 55% for 228Ra, and 84% for 210Pb in GCT high-efficiency counting mode. The total analysis time was less than 24 h, demonstrating the method's suitability for both routine monitoring and rapid response scenarios. The procedure was successfully applied to diverse environmental samples, such as rainwater surface waters, groundwater, sediments, process liquids and treated effluents. Radionuclide activity concentrations were highest in process liquids and treated effluents, whereas surface and rainwater samples showed significantly lower levels. 228Ra activity concentrations were generally low in most monitored matrices. The results were consistent with literature data reported for uranium mining and milling sites in comparable geological and operational contexts, providing no evidence of URA radiological impact on the environment. This study reinforces the importance of rapid and accurate radionuclide monitoring to ensure environmental safety and regulatory compliance in uranium mining operations.

title: A-type granitoids as a major source of indoor radon and gamma radiation: Insights from the Punilla valley (Argentina)
description: Publication date: May 2026 Source: Journal of Environmental Radioactivity, Volume 296 Author(s): Sebastián Oriolo, María Natalia Maffini, Ivana L. Ozán, Cecilia G. Cantera, María Sol Sívori, Federico Esteban, Héctor Ostera
abstract: A field-based gamma ray spectrometric study was carried out in the Punilla valley (Argentina), where indoor radon anomalies were recently reported. Results show that the highest eU values correspond to the Achala and Capilla del Monte granitoids, in contrast to their host rocks (i.e., metasedimentary and granitic rocks) and overlying Quaternary deposits, which show generally low eU concentrations. A weak, yet statistically significant positive correlation was obtained between eU and previously published indoor 222Rn data, suggesting a strong lithological control on indoor radon. In the particular case of the Achala batholith, a well-defined positive correlation was also observed between eU and 222Rn concentration based on in situ measurements using an accumulation chamber. The studied uranium-bearing intrusions mainly correspond to A-type granitoids, in line with granitoid geochemical evidence of the GEOROC database, which shows that U-bearing granitoids (i.e., U ≥ 5 mg/kg) worldwide have a typical alkaline affinity and are emplaced in post-orogenic, extensional arc or intraplate settings. When assessing the radon risk based on the geologic hazard, regions characterized by A-type magmatism can thus be considered radon-prone areas. Areas with A-type granitoids are not only radon-prone but, in general, yield relatively high natural radiation levels of multiple sources, thus highlighting the need of systematic studies to identify potentially harmful exposure.

title: Noble gas diffusion in tuff: Effects of temperature and pressure investigated with a modified time-lag method
description: Publication date: May 2026 Source: Journal of Environmental Radioactivity, Volume 296 Author(s): Guohui Wang, Elizabeth H. Denis, April J. Carman
abstract: Noble gas transport through geologic media has important applications in the characterization of underground nuclear explosions. However, transport of noble gases from the source to the surface is a complex process relying on the advective and diffusive processes in a fractured porous medium to bring detectable levels to the surface. To better understand the diffusion process in relevant porous lithofacies, laboratory experiments are necessary to characterize the diffusion of noble gas from rock fractures to the surrounding rock matrix and through porous lithofacies. In this study, a time-lag method using a chromatographic column based on Fick's law was developed and used to measure krypton and xenon diffusion through crushed (fragmented) tuff in the presence of a background gas (N2) under different temperatures and pressures. The results show that the noble gas diffusivity in tuff material increases with temperature and decreases with pressure. The noble gases with lower elemental mass and radius demonstrated greater diffusivity. These findings indicate that predictions of noble gas transport in the post-explosion subsurface geologic media should account for the effects of pressure and temperature on noble gas diffusivity.

title: The uptake and persistence of radioactive strontium in the calcified tissues of marine organisms of the Fukushima coastal region
description: Publication date: May 2026 Source: Journal of Environmental Radioactivity, Volume 296 Author(s): Hiroyuki Kintsu, Keita Kodama, Toshihiro Horiguchi
abstract: We analyzed the calcified tissues of marine organisms for accumulated 90Sr derived from the 2011 Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant (FDNPP) accident. In fish, using the spiny rasp skate Okamejei kenojei, which reportedly exhibited relatively high 90Sr concentrations among fish, we examined temporal changes in 90Sr levels in vertebrae and found a gradual decreasing trend, although 90Sr was still detectable in 2015. The average body weight of individuals with detectable 90Sr showed an increasing trend over time, and individuals with high body weight were no longer observed as the years passed, indicating that gradual decrease of 90Sr is likely due to the growth dilution and natural mortality related to their lifespan. Meanwhile, some individuals with high 90Sr concentration detected in 2013 had not been observed thereafter, which may be attributed to the other factors such as the mortality caused by the effects of highly contaminated water from FDNPP or the emigration to other areas. In invertebrates, a comprehensive analysis of accumulated 90Sr in the calcified tissues of various invertebrates revealed high levels in the Japanese common starfish Asterias amurensis. Higher 90Sr were detected in younger individuals. In addition, the estimated maximum absorbed dose rate of 90Sr into soft tissues was 170.4 μGy/d, that is too low to cause acute death. These suggest that A. amurensis was exposed to highly contaminated water during its early life stages.

title: Radiological impact from NORM discharges in the North Sea – A comparative study of aquatic modelling approaches and their implications for environmental protection
description: Publication date: May 2026 Source: Journal of Environmental Radioactivity, Volume 296 Author(s): A. Tacu, G. de With, B. Mayer, R. Bezhenar, V. Maderich
abstract: This study examines the radiological impact of naturally occurring radionuclides discharged with produced water from offshore oil and gas platforms in the North Sea. To assess the impact, two modelling approaches were compared: the compartmental model POSEIDON-R and the hydrodynamic model THREETOX. POSEIDON-R, traditionally used for large-scale assessments, divides the marine environment into interconnected “boxes” governed by mass-balance equations. In this study, its resolution was enhanced by introducing micro-compartments to capture near-field behaviour. THREETOX, in contrast, solves the Reynolds-averaged Navier–Stokes equations, providing a detailed three-dimensional simulation of plume dispersion, salinity and temperature stratification, and sediment interactions. Results show that while concentrations and doses are small, near-field hydrodynamics have a major influence. Within 3 km of the discharge point, estimated dose rates to non-human biota varied by up to six orders of magnitude depending on the model and the physical properties of the discharge. The hydrodynamic model captured localized areas of elevated concentrations of naturally occurring radionuclides missed by standard compartment models, although the refined POSEIDON-R with micro-compartments yielded improved agreement. Long-term simulations (40 years) showed sediment-dwelling species such as polychaete worms receiving the highest dose – up to about 1.8 μGy h−1 from radium-226, or 4.0 μGy h−1 when including radium-228, lead-210 and polonium-210 – but remain well below ICRP's derived consideration reference level of 400 μGy h−1 for worms. The study concludes that simplified compartmental models remain practical for prospective assessments. Nevertheless, accurate near-field evaluation requires refined or nested models, guided by hydrodynamic data. Furthermore, assessments should include long-term modelling of ecological exposure scenarios, due to radionuclide accumulation in the sediment.

title: Radioecological assessment of uranium isotopes in the soil-plant transfer process of the Hail Region, Saudi Arabia: Bioaccumulation, translocation, and exposure doses
description: Publication date: May 2026 Source: Journal of Environmental Radioactivity, Volume 296 Author(s): Othman A. Fallatah, Mahmoud R. Khattab
abstract: This study presents a radiochemical and analytical assessment of uranium isotopes (238U and 234U) in selected edible plants collected from agricultural farms in the Hail region, Saudi Arabia, an area characterized by heterogeneous geological conditions that may influence uranium mobility. Commonly consumed crops, including green pepper, lemon, eggplant, clover, mint, fig, Narenj (bitter orange), dates, herbs and pomegranate, were analyzed. Uranium isotopes were quantified using radiochemical separation followed by alpha spectrometry, providing high sensitivity, accuracy, and isotope-specific determination. The analytical method demonstrated reliable performance for environmental samples, enabling the determination of low-level uranium activities in plant tissues. The applied method achieved consistent chemical yields and low minimum detectable activities, demonstrating its suitability for low-level uranium determination in food matrices. Measured activity concentrations varied considerably among plant species and tissues, reflecting differences in soil properties, uptake mechanisms, and species-dependent accumulation behavior. To evaluate potential radiological implications, Daily Intake, Annual Effective Dose, and Committed Effective Dose were estimated using standard consumption scenarios. The calculated doses were generally below internationally recommended reference levels, indicating limited radiological concern. Soil-to-plant transfer factors (TFs) were determined to assess uranium mobility from soil to vegetation. The TF values for both isotopes were typically low in edible fruits, suggesting restricted translocation to consumable tissues. Higher TFs were observed in leafy vegetables and root tissues, particularly in mint roots, indicating enhanced uranium bioavailability under certain soil-plant conditions. Consistently higher TFs for 234U compared to 238U were attributed to the greater environmental mobility of 234U. This work provides robust analytical data and baseline information for uranium isotope distribution in food crops, supporting environmental monitoring and food safety assessments in uranium-influenced agricultural regions.

title: A Python implementation of the upgraded χ-mapping TERESA model for 210 Pb dating of recent sediments: Software and case studies
description: Publication date: May 2026 Source: Journal of Environmental Radioactivity, Volume 296 Author(s): J.M. Abril-Hernández
abstract: The 210Pb dating method enables the absolute age determination of recent sediments on a centennial scale. The Time Estimates from Random Entries of Sediments and Activities (TERESA) model addresses common sedimentary scenarios characterized by ideal deposition, absence of post-depositional redistribution, and simultaneous but independent variability in sedimentation rates and initial activity concentrations. TERESA is a χ-mapping model—a novel methodological approach that uses numerical computations across a large set (∼106) of potential solvers, representing diverse sedimentary conditions, to identify the one that minimizes a χ2 function. Although the model's fundamentals and numerous applications, including validations with varved sediments, have been previously presented, the lack of user-friendly and freely available software has limited its broader adoption by the scientific community. This work aims to present an upgraded version of TERESA supported by numerical codes written in Python and freely available on GitHub and Zenodo. It includes an updated treatment of confidence intervals, the use of normal and lognormal distributions, and objective functions that incorporate reference dates. Model performance is demonstrated using a set of cores from the literature with independent chronologies or time markers. The main advantages over classical models are discussed. The work provides novel numerical tools that enable fresh insight into the 210Pb-based dating of recent sediments.

title: Spatiotemporal variation in radiocesium concentrations under low-flow conditions in urban water bodies in Fukushima Prefecture, Japan
description: Publication date: May 2026 Source: Journal of Environmental Radioactivity, Volume 296 Author(s): Nobuhiro Suzuki, Yoshifumi Wakiyama, Hyoe Takata
abstract: This study measured 137Cs activity concentrations in water bodies in an urban area affected by the Fukushima Dai-ichi Nuclear Power Plant accident. Water samples were collected at 17 locations in five surveys conducted between August 2023 and August 2024 in Koriyama, central Fukushima Prefecture, Japan. Particulate 137Cs activity concentrations ranged from 318 to 6930 Bq/kg, with dissolved 137Cs activity concentrations of 1.62–100 mBq/L. The normalized particulate and dissolved 137Cs activity concentrations in 12 catchments, calculated by dividing the 137Cs concentration by the catchment 137Cs inventory, were 0.00352–0.0462 m2/kg and 1.25–39.3 × 10−5/m, respectively. Mean normalized dissolved 137Cs activity concentrations were generally high in locations with larger proportions of built-up areas within the catchment. Normalized dissolved 137Cs activity concentrations were higher in summer and lower in winter, with the normalized particulate 137Cs activity concentration reaching a peak in May 2024. Seasonal patterns in the spatial distribution of normalized dissolved 137Cs activity concentrations appeared to depend on those in electrical conductivity. Normalized particulate 137Cs activity concentrations were not correlated with stable nitrogen isotope signatures (δ15N) and were not positively correlated with lead content in May 2024. These results indicate that the high particulate 137Cs activity concentrations detected in May 2024 were not related to urban effects.

title: Radiological contamination in soils near the world's largest rare earth minerals producing region and their impacts on human health: A summary analysis
description: Publication date: May 2026 Source: Journal of Environmental Radioactivity, Volume 296 Author(s): Amir Hamza, Faisal Khan, Javed Nawab, Junaid Ghani, Sajid Ali, Yaseen Laghari, Luo Xin, Niaz Muhammad, Jing Cui, Zhenggui Wei
abstract: Rare earth elements (REE) mining has caused serious pollution by releasing radionuclides into the surrounding soils. Uranium and Thorium series radionuclides are geochemically linked to REE mineralization, their mobilization during mining produces persistent radiological risks that often exceed those posed by heavy metals. However, previous research has mostly focused on heavy metal contamination in REE mining soils or radiological contamination of limited locations, which may not provide a comprehensive understanding of the overall soil pollution situation in world's largest rare earth minerals-producing countries. To address this gap, our study collected and examined data from published items on REE mining and radionuclide pollution in China and Vietnam between 1993 and 2025. This research classified REE mining into two types: ion-adsorption (IA) and non-ion-adsorption (NIA). The activity concentration of 226Ra, 232Th, 40K, and 238U in the soils of these countries were analyzed, and meta-analysis was employed to assess the radiological hazards and associated health risks. The mean activity concentration value for 238U, 226Ra, 232Th, and 40K in IA and NIA REE mining soils exceeded the UNSCEAR permissible limit by 4.7, 5.1, 9.1, and 1.1 times, and 5.0, 5.0, 15, and 2.3 times, respectively. The studied soils were found to have moderate to heavy contamination levels based on radium equivalent hazard index (Ra eq ). Several radiological hazard indices, including the internal and external hazard index (H in and H ex ), absorbed gamma dose rate in the air (D air ), annual effective dose rate (AEDE), annual gonadal equivalent dose (AGED), and excess lifetime cancer risk (ELCR), exceeded the recommended limits. These findings provide valuable insights for policymakers to develop effective strategies to minimize soil radionuclide exposure.

title: Interfacial processes and biogeochemical cycling of plutonium in environmental media: Sources, transformation, and impacts
description: Publication date: May 2026 Source: Journal of Environmental Radioactivity, Volume 296 Author(s): Chun Zhang, Xiang Zhou, Hao Sun, Zengyan Li, Yu Wang, Jia Zhan, Weixian Wang, Hui Xu
abstract: Plutonium (Pu), an anthropogenic actinide with extreme radiotoxicity and chemotoxicity, derives mainly from nuclear weapons testing, accidents, and legacy waste disposal. Its environmental mobility and long-term fate are controlled by coupled interfacial reactions and biogeochemical cycling in soils, sediments, and aquatic systems. This review integrates recent advances in Pu sources, speciation, and distribution, with emphasis on adsorption–desorption at mineral–water interfaces, redox transformations across Pu(III/IV/V/VI) states, and colloid/nanoparticle-facilitated transport. Critical controls (pH, redox potential (Eh), dissolved organic matter, Fe/Mn (hydr)oxides, and microbial activity) are systematically evaluated. Microbial redox cycling, biological uptake, and immobilization pathways are shown to profoundly influence Pu speciation and transfer across environmental compartments. A unified conceptual model is presented to link interfacial processes with biogeochemical cycling under varying geochemical and climatic conditions. Current remediation technologies are critically assessed, revealing limitations and emerging interface- and microbe-targeted strategies. This synthesis provides a mechanistic framework for enhanced predictive modeling, risk assessment, and sustainable management of Pu-contaminated sites worldwide.

title: Radium recovery from mining tailings: A comprehensive review of techniques and applications
description: Publication date: May 2026 Source: Journal of Environmental Radioactivity, Volume 296 Author(s): Osman Cesar Granada Galvis, Leandro Goulart de Araujo, Roberto Vicente, Sabine Neusatz Guilhen
abstract: Radium, a naturally occurring radioactive element, has been historically recognized for its medical and industrial applications. However, with the advent of synthetic radioactive iso-topes, radium's prominence declined, and the former radium sealed sources were relegated to radioactive waste. Recent developments include the potential of radium to be used as target in a nuclear reaction to produce a radioisotope used in nuclear medicine. This has prompted the retrieval of radium sources from radioactive waste storage facilities and renewed attention on radium recovery from mining/milling residues. This review explores radium's historical significance, chemical properties, and isotopic characteristics while addressing contemporary challenges in radium extraction and applications. Particular focus is given to radium recovery techniques from residues of uranium, thorium, and rare earth element processing, emphasizing their environmental implications and regulatory considerations. The analysis highlights advancements in radium separation methods, such as ion exchange, co-precipitation, and chromatographic techniques, as well as emerging technologies aimed at optimizing recovery while mitigating environmental risks posed by mining and milling waste. By consolidating current knowledge, this study underscores the dual importance of radium recovery in resource sustainability and environmental stewardship.
