This study highlighted debris-flow impacts on sediment connectivity and the synergistic control of multiple factors on catchment-scale sediment transport to guide soil and water conservation practices in debris-flow-prone regions.

title: A climate-informed nonstationary trivariate drought index for regional assessment in Jiangsu Province, China
description: Publication date: June 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 65 Author(s): Changzhi Yu, Yunhong Hu, Xingchen Wei, Daode Gong
abstract: Study region Jiangsu Province, eastern China, characterized by a humid monsoon climate, dense river networks, intensive water use, and strong interactions among precipitation, runoff, and groundwater. Study focus This study develops a climate-informed Nonstationary Trivariate Standardized Drought Index (NTSDI) to characterize compound drought dynamics under changing hydroclimatic conditions. Precipitation, surface runoff, and groundwater are integrated within a unified probabilistic framework. Large-scale climate indices are incorporated as explanatory variables to account for climate-driven nonstationarity. Nonstationary marginal distributions are modeled using Generalized Additive Models for Location, Scale, and Shape, while a time-varying D-vine copula is applied to capture evolving multivariate dependence structures. New hydrological insights for the region Results reveal a significant hydroclimatic regime shift around 2003 across precipitation, surface runoff, and subsurface runoff. Compared with the pre-change period, precipitation decreased by 8.78%, surface runoff by 20.98%, and subsurface runoff by 36.89%, indicating amplified drought propagation from atmospheric input to subsurface hydrological response. The NTSDI effectively captures compound drought evolution and delayed subsurface hydrological responses, providing a more robust basis for regional drought monitoring than conventional indices. By explicitly accounting for climate-driven nonstationarity and multivariate dependence, it offers valuable support for drought risk assessment and adaptive water resources management in highly dynamic hydroclimatic regions such as Jiangsu Province.

title: Research on forecasting of diverse flood types based on the deep learning of sub-modal features in high-altitude mountainous basin
description: Publication date: June 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 65 Author(s): Xuyang Shi, Jiao Liu, Haidong Liang, Gonghuan Fang, Tie Liu, Xi Chen
abstract: Study region Kaidu River Basin, where located within the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, is one of the four major tributaries of the Tarim River. Study focus This study examines the challenges in forecasting nonlinear and nonstationary flood processes, with particular emphasis on high-altitude mountainous watersheds.Based on the observed daily runoff data from 1959 to 2018 at the Dashankou Hydrological Station and the extracted 152 flood events by POT (Peaks Over Threshold) method. A hybrid model combining VMD(Variational Mode Decomposition) and LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory) was developed to flood simulate and forecast without any future referenceinformation, and analyze the role of different sub-modal decomposition features in runoff sequence. New hydrological insights for the region After Bayesian optimization, both the standalone LSTM and the hybrid VMD-LSTM models achieved excellent performance in simulating runoff sequences, with R² values of 0.99 and 0.93, respectively. The VMD-LSTM model significantly reduces the complexity of runoff signals by decomposing them into multiple sub-modal components across low- to high-frequency bands, This decomposition enhances the model’s ability to capture the dynamics of flood events. Notably, the VMD-LSTM model achieves an 88.2% same-day peak discharge detection rate, substantially outperforming the standalone LSTM model, which only reaches 2.6%. Through the sub-model characteristics from low to high frequencies, the hybrid model hierarchically resolves the determinism of runoff accumulation and the uncertainty of short-term fluctuations during flood development. Even without access to future observational data, it can still effectively capture the flood evolution process, and At all four forecasting horizons—1, 5, 10, and 15 days—it consistently exhibits lower cumulative errors than the single LSTM model. While the LSTM model performed well in capturing the overall runoff regime in high-altitude mountain basins, its integration with the VMD significantly improved flood event detection and forecasting performance. This hybrid framework provides valuable scientific insights for improving mountain flood early warning and defense strategies.

title: Dynamic D-vine copula GAM quantile regression for boosting probabilistic streamflow forecasting reliability
description: Publication date: June 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 65 Author(s): Hongtao Dong, Jungang Luo, Ganggang Zuo, Xue Yang
abstract: Study Region The Hanjiang River Basin, China Study Focus Reliable and accurate streamflow forecasting is essential for effective water resources management, flood mitigation, and hydrological risk assessment. Deterministic forecasting approaches provide point predictions only and therefore fail to explicitly represent predictive uncertainty. To address this limitation and enhance forecast reliability, this study develops a probabilistic post-processing framework that transforms deep learning-based point forecasts (LSTM and Transformer) into probability forecasts by modeling the conditional error structure. The framework models forecast errors as the response variable and captures their regime-dependent dependence on hydrometeorological covariates using a dynamic D-vine copula generalized additive model quantile regression (DV-GAM-QR), enabling the generation of both median forecasts and probabilistic prediction intervals. New Hydrological Insights The proposed DV-GAM-QR framework substantially improves probabilistic streamflow forecasting by explicitly modeling time-varying dependence between deep-learning forecast errors and hydrometeorological predictors. Compared with the stationary DVQR benchmark, DV-GAM-QR achieves marked gains in probabilistic performance, reducing the Continuous Ranked Probability Score (CRPS) by approximately 15% and producing sharper yet well-calibrated prediction intervals across flow regimes. This study demonstrates that forecast error dependence is not merely non-stationary over time, but rather varies systematically as a function of seasonal conditions and antecedent hydrologic memory. By integrating hydrologically meaningful covariates into a dynamic copula parameterization, the framework reveals regime-dependent dependence patterns that are obscured under stationary assumptions. These findings highlight the importance of dynamic dependence modeling for reliable uncertainty quantification and illustrate how copula-based post-processing can be effectively coupled with deep learning outputs to support risk-sensitive streamflow forecasting and water resources management.

title: Enhancing groundwater resilience through ecological compensation: A pathway for sustainable water resource management in China
description: Publication date: June 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 65 Author(s): Ming-yuan Ji, Yang Xu, Zhuo-xun Wu, Li-yang Feng, Xu Duan, Meng-xi He, Li He
abstract: Study region 192 major Chinese cities where groundwater accounts for more than 10% of total water supply during 2001–2020, covering major hydrogeological settings, including the North China Plain aquifer system, alluvial aquifers of the Yangtze River Basin, and karst aquifers in southwestern China. Study focus This study develops an emergy-based assessment framework to quantify ecological compensation requirements associated with groundwater extraction. The framework integrates time-dependent allocation of environmental losses with the conversion of water conservation potential to evaluate the environmental costs of groundwater overexploitation and support sustainable groundwater management at the urban scale. New hydrological insights for the region Groundwater extraction induces substantial hydrological and ecological impacts, including land subsidence, groundwater pollution, vegetation deterioration, seawater intrusion, and surface runoff reduction. Emergy-based assessment reveals that cumulative environmental losses reached 9.75 × 1023 sej between 2001 and 2020, with land subsidence accounting for the dominant share (6.41 × 1023 sej). The results reveal pronounced spatial heterogeneity in ecosystem losses across hydrogeological settings, reflecting differences in geological sensitivity and groundwater exploitation intensity. Futhermore, the analysis captures the temporal evolution of groundwater-related environmental pressures and indicates that ecological compensation policies, combined with water-saving measures such as winter fallowing, crop structure optimization, and improved irrigation efficiency, could reduce groundwater extraction by approximately 2.43 × 1011 m3 over a 20-year period.

title: Evolution of precipitation-runoff-sediment dependence under environmental change: A Vine Copula analysis of two Loess Plateau basins
description: Publication date: June 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 65 Author(s): Jiahui Li, Guoqing Wang, Ting Zhou
abstract: Study Region Two major sediment-yielding sub-basins of the Loess Plateau: The Kuye River and Wuding River Basins Study Focus This study investigates the multivariate evolution of precipitation-runoff-sediment (P-R-S) relationships in the Kuye and Wuding River Basins during 1958–2020. By integrating changepoint detection with a Vine Copula framework, the nonlinear, conditional, and tail dependence of P-R-S structures are quantified, and their stage-wise evolution under climate variability and soil and water conservation measures is traced. New hydrological insights for the region Results reveal a systematic strengthening of precipitation-runoff coupling in both basins, with upper-tail dependence coefficients increasing to as high as 0.98, indicating enhanced runoff sensitivity to extreme rainfall. In contrast, runoff-sediment relationships diverge markedly between basins. In the Kuye River Basin, Kendall’s τ decreases from 0.80 to 0.65, reflecting a transition from rainfall-driven to supply-limited sediment yield as sediment sources is progressively depleted by long-term conservation conservation. The Wuding River Basin exhibits a nonlinear collapse-recovery trajectory of runoff-sediment dependence, associated with heterogeneous geomorphic conditions and spatially variable effects of check dams and vegetation restoration. Conditional dependence analysis further indicates a shift from energy-limited to material-limited erosion regimes under fixed runoff conditions, particularly during low-flow periods. Overall, the results provide quantitative evidence that large-scale ecological restoration has fundamentally reshaped hydrological-sedimentary interactions on the Loess Plateau.

title: A flow constrained simplification method for high-resolution fracture networks in epikarst zone
description: Publication date: June 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 65 Author(s): Fengjun Gao, Xi Chen, Zhicai Zhang, Yingchun Liang, Weihan Liu
abstract: Study region The study was conducted within Puding County, Guizhou Province. Study focus Karst regions are widely covered by fractured aquifers. These fracture networks often exhibit complex structures, making simulations of flow and solute transport computationally expensive and numerically unstable. This severely limits our ability to quantify and characterize uncertainties in karst fracture systems. This study proposes a simplification method for high-resolution fracture networks extracted from field outcrops. The performance and applicability of the proposed method are evaluated using natural fracture networks with varying structural complexity and scales. New Hydrological Insights for the Region Numerical simulations on four natural fracture networks indicate that, although high-resolution fracture models provide detailed geometric information, not all geometric details exert a controlling influence on macroscopic hydraulic responses. Excessive geometric refinement yields limited improvement in hydraulic representation, while substantially increasing mesh density and degrees of freedom, thereby reducing computational efficiency. The proposed flow-constrained simplification method reduces local structural complexity while effectively preserving the dominant flow pathways and equivalent permeability. Solute transport simulations further demonstrate that, under appropriately selected thresholds, breakthrough curve deviations remain within acceptable limits and are significantly smaller than those obtained using unconstrained geometric simplification, particularly for structurally complex networks. The proposed method provides a physically grounded and computationally efficient framework for reducing model complexity without compromising key hydrological processes.

title: Impacts of underground structures on the hydrological functions of urban green spaces
description: Publication date: June 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 65 Author(s): Yao Wang, Weiguang Wang, Quanxi Shao, Meng Ding, Xiang Zhang, Shijie Cao
abstract: Study region A typical urban residential compound in China. Equipped with an extensive underground parking. With considerable green space area providing potential benefits of runoff mitigation via imperviousness disconnection. Study focus This study focuses on the impacts of the underground parking structure on the hydrological processes and the green space functions. Using a fully-distributed and coupled surface-subsurface model, we analyzed the changes in soil saturation, runoff, and evapotranspiration caused by the underground structure. New hydrological insights for the region Results show that the underground parking structure causes soil water accumulation on its top in long term, leading to higher runoff and evapotranspiration. The magnitude of these effects relies on water supply to the green space. Lower water supply (e.g., when the climate is dryer or soil permeability is lower) would result in less soil water accumulation, thereby weakening the hydrological effects. In contrast, these effects are amplified when imperviousness disconnection is implemented, as it increases water supply to the green space through focused infiltration. Moreover, for the condition of imperviousness disconnection, these effects are not confined to the disconnection point, as the water accumulation zone can develop via subsurface lateral preferential flow along the underground parking slab, potentially influencing runoff generation patterns over a larger area. These findings highlight the importance of considering urban underground structure in stormwater management, especially for regions with wet climate.

title: Optimizing flood susceptibility mapping using GIS-based frequency ratio and analytic hierarchy process: A case study in Thailand
description: Publication date: June 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 65 Author(s): Nanthaporn Usaard, Panuwit Boonnan, Jedsadaporn Nonbudsri, Komsan Kiriwongwattana, Sopa Cansee
abstract: Study region Ubon Ratchathani Province in Northeastern Thailand, located within the Mun–Chi–Lower Mekong River system, is highly prone to recurrent monsoon-driven flooding. Study focus This study applies a comparative GIS-based framework integrating the Frequency Ratio (FR), Relative Frequency Ratio (RFR), and Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) to evaluate flood susceptibility across the province. Nine conditioning factors were analyzed, including elevation, rainfall, slope, soil drainage, land use, stream density, road density, and proximity to streams and roads. Model performance was assessed using Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curves and Area Under the Curve (AUC) metrics. New hydrological insights for the region The AHP model demonstrated the highest predictive capability (AUC = 0.87), followed by RFR (0.82) and FR (0.78). Rainfall, elevation, and distance from streams were identified as the dominant determinants of flood susceptibility, whereas land-use type and road density exhibited lower influence. The AHP model produced more spatially coherent high-risk zones compared with the more fragmented outputs of FR and RFR. These results provide spatially explicit evidence to support flood-mitigation prioritization, infrastructure planning, and provincial disaster-risk governance. The combined data-driven and expert-driven framework demonstrates strong transferability to other monsoon-influenced basins in the Mekong region and contributes to long-term hydrological adaptation strategies.

title: Accelerated glacier retreat in the Irtysh River Basin (Kazakhstan) during 1993–2022
description: Publication date: June 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 65 Author(s): Xingran Cai, Jiayi Liu, Chunhai Xu, Feiteng Wang, Zhonghua He
abstract: Study region The Irtysh River Basin in Kazakhstan Study focus In recent decades, global warming has driven widespread yet spatially heterogeneous glacier retreat worldwide. Here, we utilize multi-source remote sensing data to investigate glacier changes in the Irtysh River Basin of Kazakhstan from 1993 to 2022, and analyze the climatic driving factors behind these changes. New hydrological insights for the region Our results show that the Irtysh River Basin (Kazakhstan) hosted 285 glaciers covering 113.62 ± 12.79 km² in 1993. By 2022, the region had lost 21 glaciers, and the total glacier area shrank to 75.84 ± 9.41 km², representing a loss of 37.78 ± 3.38 km². The total ice volume declined by 1.81 ± 0.07 km³ , equivalent to about 31.87% of the 1993 vol. Glacier retreat was predominantly concentrated in small-sized and north-facing glaciers. Overall, glaciers experienced fluctuating but accelerating retreat from 1993 to 2022. A pronounced acceleration occurred during 2001–2006, and the retreat rate intensified again in the most recent period of 2016–2022 with a rate of −1.49 km² a⁻¹ , approximately twice that of the 1990s. Temperature rise was the primary driver of accelerating glacier retreat in the lower Irtysh River basin over the past three decades.

title: Water balance–based evaluation and attribution of multi-source evapotranspiration datasets in the Qinling–Daba Mountains, China
description: Publication date: June 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 65 Author(s): Yanhong Tang, Yi He, Rui Yan
abstract: Study region The Qinling–Daba Mountains, China. Study focus Due to the complex topography and heterogeneous climatic conditions of the Qinling–Daba (Qinba) Mountains, substantial uncertainties remain among evapotranspiration (ET) datasets with varying spatial and temporal resolutions. In this study, we evaluated 18 ET datasets using the water balance and Triple Collocation, investigated the factors influencing their accuracy through Spearman's rank correlation analysis across the Qinba Mountains. New hydrogeological insights from the region In the Qinba Mountains, most ET datasets exhibit a distinct spatial pattern of lower values in the northwest and higher values in the southeast, with annual ET ranging from 400 to 850 mm·yr⁻¹ and clustering around 600 mm·yr⁻¹ , accompanied by pronounced seasonal and interannual variability. Among the evaluated datasets, GLEAM4 demonstrates the highest overall performance at both monthly and seasonal scales, followed by PML_V2, GLASS, and ET_CR, with all datasets performing better during wet seasons than dry seasons. From 2007–2017, most datasets show strong consistency in interannual variations, particularly a common fluctuation during 2013–2014, indicating high reliability in capturing regional ET dynamics. Topographic complexity is identified as the dominant factor limiting ET model accuracy, whereas climatic energy conditions exert a positive influence on model performance. Overall, this study provides a reference for the selection of ET datasets in the Qinba Mountains and other mountainous regions characterized by complex terrain and climatic heterogeneity.

title: Numerical simulation of freeze-up process and optimized ice boom deployment in a natural river reach
description: Publication date: June 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 65 Author(s): Suming Li, Chao Li, Hung Tao Shen, Shengjie Cui, Huiping Hou
abstract: Study region Inner Mongolia section of the Yellow River, China. Study focus Investigate the river freeze-up process under different ice-boom layouts and flow regulation schemes to reduce the potential of breakup ice-jam flooding. The variations in freeze-up length and ice thickness under different working conditions are analyzed, and the optimal ice-boom layout and flow regulation scheme for smooth, stable freeze-up covers are determined. New hydrological insights for the region The Inner Mongolia reach of the Yellow River is often affected by spring ice-jam flooding. Installing ice booms in river channels allows cover formation during freeze-up, reducing the ice mass in the channel and the potential for breakup ice-jam flooding. However, the boom installation must be coordinated with the flow and weather conditions to be effective. For example, the analysis showed that when a full-width ice boom is installed at the Huhhot-Jungar Railway Bridge, and upstream discharge is regulated to 350 m³ /s during a four-day freeze-up ice run, it enables the formation of ice cover over 66% of the reach upstream. This condition performs favorably in terms of freeze-up length, cover thickness, and reduced open-water area for winter ice production. This study provides theoretical and technical support for ice jam flood prevention in the reach and a method for possible application to rivers in cold regions.

title: Characterizing the impacts of Climate Change and Human activities to wetland suitability in a mid-high latitude region
description: Publication date: June 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 65 Author(s): Jianmiao Wang, Weijia Hu, Jiaxin Yu, Dandan Zhao, Jiping Liu
abstract: Study region The Greater Khingan Mountains, located in northeastern China, is a key region for mid- high latitudes wetlands. Study focus This study proposes a novel multi-scenario simulation based on the MaxEnt model that simultaneously considered single and coupled spatial impacts of climate change and human activities on wetland suitability during 2021–2100. Quantitative analysis indicated that river proximity, slope, climatic factors and human activities were the key drivers of current wetland distribution. New hydrological insight Results indicated that wetland areas expanded by 9.84–11.13% under the SSP1–2.6 and SSP2–4.5 scenarios during 2021–2040, but decreased to 8.23% under the SSP5–8.5 scenario during 2071–2100. Under the climate change-human activities coupled scenarios, the combined effects reduced wetland expansion rates by 1.64–3.43% compared with climate change-single scenarios under SSP1–2.6 and SSP2–4.5 scenarios during 2021–2100. Under scenarios of human activities disturbance, the inhibiting impacts of human activities on wetland expansion intensified under SSP5–8.5 scenario during 2021–2100 and wetland expansion rate decreased by 5.52% compared to the climate change-single scenarios. Overall, climate change altered wetland suitability primarily while human activities significantly amplified the influence under all emission scenarios. Especially, the coupled effects of climate change and human activities exacerbated wetland contraction and suppressed expansion under SSP5–8.5 scenario. This study provides scientific support for conservation and management of wetlands in mid-high latitudes influenced by climate change and human activities.

title: Monitoring agricultural drought in Xinjiang, China, using the climatic precipitation evapotranspiration index
description: Publication date: June 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 65 Author(s): Hao Tang, Qiao Li, Hongfei Tao, Pingan Jiang, Xiangzhi Kong, YuXin Wei, Yong Peng
abstract: Study area Xinjiang, China. Study focus The Agricultural Productivity Ratio (APR) was combined with the cumulative distribution function of water deficit (WD) to construct the climatic precipitation evapotranspiration index (CPEI). Furthermore, the SPEI_3, standardized soil moisture index (SSI), and vegetation condition index (VCI) were calculated. The accuracy of these four indices and their associated drought evolution trends was compared and assessed using Pearson correlation analysis, actual agricultural drought data, Theil-Sen estimator, Mann-Kendall test, and spatial transfer matrix. New hydrological insights for the region The results indicate that CPEI_3 outperforms conventional indices in capturing agricultural drought dynamics across Xinjiang's diverse climates. This enhanced performance is evidenced by stronger correlations with soil moisture (r = 0.59) and NDVI compared to SPEI_3 and SSI. Notably, while VCI ranks highest in spatial accuracy, it tends to misclassify drought as non-drought, underscoring CPEI_3's superior reliability. The drought severity trajectory reveals a distinct weakening, intensifying, and weakening pattern, with 48.52% of the region exhibiting slight worsening. These findings demonstrate considerable potential for advancing agricultural drought monitoring and assessment practices.

title: Summer monsoon precipitation patterns and their relationship to flood probabilities across Pakistan
description: Publication date: June 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 65 Author(s): Mohib Ullah, Chenghai Wang, Safi Ullah, Esha Malik, Mushtaq Ahmad Jan, Ali Naqi
abstract: Study region In Pakistan, the climate crisis manifests most dangerously through extreme monsoon precipitation and subsequent flooding. Study focus To quantify the relationship between summer monsoon precipitation and flood probability, the study establishes and applies Intensity-Duration-Frequency (IDF) and Quantile-Duration-Frequency (QDF) frameworks. These frameworks utilize ERA5 precipitation data and multi-source streamflow records from 1950 to 2024 to assess extreme events across Pakistan. New hydrological insights for the region Results reveal noticeable spatial variation in flood sensitivity across Pakistan. The northern mountainous regions exhibit the highest vulnerability to flooding, characterized by extreme precipitation magnitudes exceeding 25 mm/hr for 1-hr events and the highest streamflow elasticity (ε₁ up to 0.33 for 2-yrs and 0.35 for 100-yrs return periods), indicating that flood peaks increase proportionally with precipitation intensity. The Central and Eastern regions show moderate elasticity ε₁ up to 0.27 and 0.22, respectively. In contrast, the Southern region exhibits minimal flood probability/sensitivity (elasticity ∼0.17), instead highlighting critical water scarcity. Flooding is primarily driven by short-duration (1–3 hrs) extreme summer monsoon precipitation exceeding 30 mm/hr in the Northern region and is characterized by a coherence between precipitation and streamflow peaks of more than 70%. The elasticity ratio ε₂, representing the alignment between storm duration and catchment response, is highest in the North (∼0.60) and lowest in the South (∼0.17), confirming the influence of terrain morphology on flood-generation efficiency. These findings highlight the critical need for region-specific flood risk strategies, including early warning systems in high-sensitivity Northern areas and water retention measures in arid Western regions of Pakistan.

title: Spatial heterogeneity and multivariate drivers of flood hazard in data-scarce small watersheds
description: Publication date: June 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 65 Author(s): Nijuan Yang, Ting Zhang, Jianzhu Li, Ping Feng, Changjun Zhu
abstract: Study region The study area focuses on 15 small watersheds in Shanxi Province, China, spanning the Yongding, Ziya, and Zhangwei river systems. These watersheds are located in a transitional zone from semi‑arid to semi‑humid climates, with complex topography and extremely sparse hydrological data and intensive human activities. Study focus This study evaluates flood hazard conditions across the 15 watersheds by integrating hydrological methods with the Integrated Flood Modeling System (IFMS). Flood hydrographs and inundation dynamics were simulated for five return periods (5‑, 10‑, 20‑, 50‑, and 100‑year). Comparative analyses were performed across three hydrological zones and three land use types to quantify the coupled effects of natural and anthropogenic drivers on flood hazard characteristics. New hydrological insights for the region The Shizi, Mian, and Yangwu River basins exhibit the most severe flood hazards, with maximum inundation depths exceeding 2.0 m, inundated areas larger than 3.0 km², and affected populations over 1200 persons. Basins in Hydrological Zone II (semi-arid) show higher mean inundation depths (1.69 m) than those in the more humid Zone III (1.27 m), which is mainly attributed to sparse vegetation and a high impervious surface fraction (exceeding 70%). Watersheds dominated by Cropland‑Built‑up land (CBUL) show the highest vulnerability, while Forest‑Grassland (FGL) and Water‑Rich (WR) types exhibit significantly lower flood hazards. Reservoirs in Water-Rich basins notably attenuate flood impacts. These results reveal that human‑altered land use can override climatic gradients to dominate flood hazard dynamics, providing a scientific basis for spatially targeted flood mitigation strategies in data‑scarce regions.

title: Spatiotemporal evolution and driving mechanisms of agricultural drought across different spatial scales in Northeast China
description: Publication date: June 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 65 Author(s): Cangming Zhang, Lixin Wang, Guanglei Hou, Jia Du, Zhiqiang Wang, Kaishan Song, Bingrun Sui, Yu Han
abstract: Study region Northeast China (NEC), one of the world’s four major black soil regions and a key grain-producing area in China, spans a pronounced hydro-climatic gradient from humid to semi-arid conditions under a temperate continental monsoon climate. Study focus This study constructed the temperature vegetation dryness index (TVDI) for NEC during 2000–2022 to characterize agricultural drought at multiple spatial scales. The spatiotemporal patterns of drought were examined for NEC as a whole and across 12 divisions defined by geographic subregions, climate zones, and ecosystem types. In addition, the optimal parameter geographical detector (OPGD) was applied to quantify the factors controlling drought distribution and its spatiotemporal evolution. New hydrological insight From 2000–2022, TVDI decreased at a rate of −2.20 × 10−3 yr−1, indicating an overall alleviation of agricultural drought in NEC. However, drought severity showed marked spatial heterogeneity, with the Liao River Plain experiencing the most severe drought. Drought intensified from humid to semi-humid to semi-arid zones, while the wetting trend weakened accordingly. Forest ecosystems showed stronger drought resistance than grasslands and croplands. PET, land use/land cover, and temperature primarily controlled the spatial distribution of drought, whereas temperature, PET, and precipitation dominated its spatiotemporal evolution. These findings provide new hydrological evidence that agricultural drought in NEC is jointly regulated by atmospheric water demand, water supply conditions, and land surface characteristics.

title: Bridging process-based simulation and deep learning: A location-aware framework for quantifying water diversion impacts on groundwater recovery
description: Publication date: June 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 65 Author(s): Yongyu Song, Jing Zhang, Zeqi Li, Xianyong Meng
abstract: Study region North China Plain, China Study focus We propose a hybrid MODFLOW–Location-Aware LSTM (MODFLOW-LA-LSTM) framework to improve groundwater storage change prediction and support intervention attribution. MODFLOW-NWT simulations provide process-informed predictors (water-balance components and simulated storage), while an LSTM learns residual corrections to storage. “Location-aware” capability is implemented by concatenating a categorical location encoding (province/city one-hot vector) with the hydrologic feature sequence, enabling a single model to learn region-specific response patterns across basin-to-municipal scales. We then apply a counterfactual trend–deviation analysis to quantify deviations from pre-transfer groundwater trajectories associated with SNWD. New hydrological insights for the region The hybrid framework better captures spatial heterogeneity in NCP groundwater dynamics across contrasting managed settings than process-only simulations, improving the representation of both depletion phases and subsequent stabilization. The counterfactual analysis provides a bounded estimate of SNWD-associated shifts in post-2014 groundwater trajectories at regional and subregional scales, highlighting stronger and more coherent recovery signals in major receiving metropolitan areas and more variable responses in agriculturally dominated regions where concurrent management and climate variability can modulate outcomes. These results offer spatially differentiated evidence to support adaptive groundwater regulation and surface-water substitution strategies in the NCP.

title: Persistent warming and declining relative humidity drive the reversal of declining pan evaporation in Northwest China after 1990
description: Publication date: June 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 65 Author(s): Wenhui Jiang, Xinwei Deng, Bingxue Dong, Han Wang, Zhentao Bai, Kechun Wang, Zhijun Li, Junliang Fan
abstract: Study region Northwest China (NWC) experiences arid and semi-arid climates and is highly vulnerable to climate change. Study focus Global warming has intensified evaporation and exacerbated water scarcity in the (semi-)arid regions of NWC, where sparse meteorological stations and significant data deficiencies pose additional challenges. This study developed a continuous daily pan evaporation dataset of both D20 and E601 from 374 meteorological stations across NWC (1961–2020), and systematically analyzed the spatiotemporal patterns and driving factors of D20 and E601 pan evaporation across annual, freezing and non-freezing periods. The sensitivity of different pan types to key climatic variables including temperature, relative humidity, wind speed (U2), and sunshine duration (SSD) were further quantitatively analyzed. New hydrological insights for the region This study reveals a shift in pan evaporation drivers in NWC around 1990, from U2-dominated decline to temperature/humidity-driven increase, elucidating the “evaporation paradox”. Xinjiang and Gansu show increasing evaporation after 1990, while Qinghai and Northern Shaanxi show declines. D20 is more temperature-sensitive, whereas E601 responds more to U2 and SSD, explaining their divergence. These changes have direct implications for water resources management: increasing evaporation in Xinjiang and Gansu indicates higher atmospheric evaporative demand and irrigation water requirements, while declining or redistributed evaporation in Qinghai and Northern Shaanxi highlights the need for improved soil moisture conservation and optimized irrigation and water allocation.

title: A multi-source stacking framework with inverse-transformation bias correction for mapping soil salinity in arid oases: A case study from the Yarkant River Oasis
description: Publication date: June 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 65 Author(s): Shuiqing Liu, Songhao Shang
abstract: Study region The Yarkant River Oasis, Xinjiang, Northwest China, a representative arid inland oasis system. Study focus We developed a reproducible multi-source data-fusion and stacking framework with inverse-transformation bias correction to improve soil salinity mapping in arid oases, where strong spatial heterogeneity and water-salt interactions challenge conventional approaches. Applied to the study region, the RF+XGBoost stacking model achieved stable predictive performance (test R2≥0.70) and improved extrapolation reliability after bias correction. By integrating multi-source remote sensing, meteorological, and topographic variables at 300 m resolution, the framework captures both surface spectral responses and underlying hydro-environmental controls on salinity distribution. The incorporation of inverse-transformation bias correction further enhances calibration across different salinity levels, enabling more reliable identification of spatial salinity gradients and hotspots relevant to irrigation-drainage processes. New hydrological insights for the region Mean total soil salt content (TS) remained stable (2.55–2.63 g/kg) during 2021–2025 with an increase of about 1.18% in five years, indicating no dominant basin-scale trend during the spring sowing period. However, pronounced spatial divergence persists: downstream areas remain salinity hotspots, whereas several midstream and upstream counties show increasing trends (>10%), reflecting spatial differences in groundwater conditions and irrigation-drainage regimes. This pattern suggests coexistence of remediation and risk, highlighting the need for zone-specific monitoring and management in arid oasis systems.

title: A dual-TransUNet deep learning framework for multi-source precipitation merging and improving seasonal and extreme estimates
description: Publication date: June 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 65 Author(s): Yuchen Ye, Zixuan Qi, Shixuan Li, Wei Qi, Yanpeng Cai, Chaoxia Yuan
abstract: Study region China (18.0–53.5°N, 73.5–135.0°E), focusing on eastern China, where heavy-rain hazards are most severe, and the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau, where sparse gauges limit precipitation assessment. Study focus We develop DDL-MSPMF, a dual-stage deep-learning framework that merges and bias-corrects daily 0.25° precipitation over China during 2001–2020 using six multisource precipitation products and four ERA5 near-surface predictors. A classifier first identifies rainfall occurrence, and a regressor then predicts rainfall amount. Performance is evaluated against the original products and deep-learning/hybrid baselines using CN05.1 across China and TPHiPr over the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau, with additional tests for heavy-rain detection and the July 2021 Zhengzhou rainstorm. New hydrological insights for the region Separating rainfall occurrence from rainfall amount improves precipitation merging across contrasting hydroclimatic regions of China. The best model, TransUNet–TransUNet, achieves the highest seasonal skill (R = 0.7512; RMSE = 2.6954 mm/day), improves heavy-rain detection across much of eastern China, and better reproduces the Zhengzhou event than the original products and simpler baselines. These gains also extend to the data-scarce Qinghai–Tibet Plateau. Interpretation shows that rainfall-occurrence information suppresses false light-rain signals and reduces heavy-rain underestimation, while surface pressure is the most influential auxiliary predictor. The framework provides an interpretable route to improving precipitation forcing for flood monitoring and hydroclimatic risk assessment in China.

title: Climate-responsive reservoir operation for the environmental flow management of the proposed Nagmati Dam in the Bagmati basin, Nepal
description: Publication date: June 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 65 Author(s): Niroj Phuyal, Utsab Phuyal, Pratik Singh Thakuri, Amit Shrestha, Soni M. Pradhanang
abstract: Study region The study focuses on the Nagmati catchment of the Bagmati River basin, Nepal, with a focus on the proposed Nagmati Reservoir, in the vicinity of the source of the Bagmati River, located on the hills of Kathmandu valley, draining to downstream Gaurighat gauging station. Study focus This study evaluates whether calibrated operation of a reservoir can sustain downstream environmental flows (E-flows) under historical and future climates. Mean monthly flows were simulated using the Stanford Watershed Model driven by an ensemble of four CMIP6 climate projections under SSP2–4.5 and SSP5–8.5. Using the Ganga E-flow calculator, E-flow thresholds were defined for six Environmental Management Classes (EMCs). A simple spreadsheet-based reservoir operation model was applied across near future (NF), mid future (MF), and far future (FF) periods, and calibrated to sustain E-flow for EMC C (moderately modified flow) condition. New hydrological insights for the region Projected ensemble means indicate an overall increase in mean monthly inflows across future periods, with stronger increases under the high-emission scenario. The calibrated and validated model demonstrated strong seasonal flow reproduction (Nash–Sutcliffe and R² > 0.81). The mean monthly inflow to the reservoir for historical period (1995–2020) was calculated to be 0.48 m3/s. Under SSP2–4.5, simulated flows increased to 0.69, 0.74 and 0.73 m3/s for NF, MF and FF, respectively. The SSP5–8.5 simulated further increased flow trajectories of 0.62, 0.75, and 0.93 m³/s for NF, MF and FF, respectively. The reservoir operation model maintained a continuous release of 0.52 m³/s, exceeding the planned hydropower allocation of 0.45 m³/s, and met the environmental flow requirements for an EMC C (moderately modified flow). Results highlight that climate-driven increases in monsoon inflow can provide storage and operational flexibility, but intra-seasonal variability and data limitations require adaptive management and further ecological and water-quality assessments.

title: Study on the coupling mechanism and dynamic response of hydrometeorological factors and runoff in the upper reaches of the Kriya River based on the SVAR model
description: Publication date: June 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 65 Author(s): Kun Xing, Jiahui Wang, Sihai Liu
abstract: Study region The headwaters region of the Kriya River in the inland river basins of arid Northwest China. Study focus Using remote sensing and observed runoff data (2001–2019), this study applied STL decomposition and trend tests to assess multi-timescale variations in precipitation, air and land surface temperature, snow cover, soil moisture, and runoff. A physically-constrained SVAR model was subsequently constructed to discern driving mechanisms through impulse response and Forecast Error Variance Decomposition (FEVD) analyses. New hydrological insights for the region From 2001–2019, precipitation showed a weak increasing trend (Sen’s β = 0.078, p = 0.484) while runoff declined slightly (Sen’s β = −0.074, p = 0.441). Land surface and air temperatures decreased marginally; soil moisture and snow cover showed no significant trends. Precipitation dominated short-term runoff variability, accounting for 15.2% in the first period. Snow cover produced a lagged accumulation release effect that increasingly influenced medium- to long-term runoff. By period eight, air temperature together with land surface temperature explained 18.27% of runoff variance, reflecting energy control on snowmelt and release dynamics. The proposed framework, merging physical constraints, STL, SVAR responses, and FEVD, offers precise lag resolution and causal runoff diagnosis. It provides quantitative guidance for improving runoff forecasting, snowmelt management, and climate adaptation in cold, arid alpine headwaters. Its methodology is adaptable to other similar basins, supporting model calibration and water resource planning.

title: Simulation and prediction of lake water storage response to climate change in a high-cold arid region: The case of typical lakes on the northern slope of the Kunlun Mountains
description: Publication date: June 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 65 Author(s): Yuting Liu, Yaning Chen, Chenggang Zhu, Shuhua Zhang, Qifei Zhang
abstract: Study region The northern slope of the Kunlun Mountains is a high-cold arid region on the northwestern edge of the Tibetan Plateau characterized by extreme altitudes (>4500 m), low precipitation, and extensive glacier coverage (3.5%). Study focus We reconstructed past (1990–2020) and predicted future (2021–2030) responses of lake water storage to climate change for typical lakes along the northern slope of the Kunlun Mountains using multi-source satellite datasets (Landsat, altimetry, and GRACE) and back propagation (BP) neural network modeling. New hydrological insights Significant lake area expansion (+77.19%) and increases in lake number (+162.79%) were observed post-2003. Lake Ayagkumu showed the most significant increase in water storage change rate, increasing at 0.0418 km3/a post-2003 compared to −0.0071 km3/a pre-2003. Monthly-scale analysis revealed abrupt changes in lake water storage, with significant increases observed for Lake Aqqikkol in April 2003. Seasonal patterns in lake water storage were also observed, with the warm season (May–September) exhibiting peak growth. BP neural network predictions showed continued expansion for most lakes with good accuracy (±10% deviation vs. observations), confirming the good predictive capability of the model. Validation using GRACE data further confirmed model reliability (0.0895 km3/a vs. 0.0903 km3/a observed). These findings clarify hydrological processes in high-cold arid regions and serve as an important scientific basis for assessing water resource vulnerability and formulating adaptation strategies.

title: Impacts of basin-wide reservoir operations on future Yangtze river flood and flow regimes under bias-corrected CMIP6 projections
description: Publication date: June 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 65 Author(s): Ping Liu, Zexu Zhang, Li Tang, Yingna Cao
abstract: Study region The Yangtze River Basin, China. Study focus Existing studies primarily focus on the historical impacts of a few large dams at localized sites, leaving the collective impacts of basin-wide reservoir operations under future climate scenarios poorly understood. We address this gap by implementing a hydroclimate framework that incorporates 327 dams into the mizuRoute river model. We applied a water-balance-based bias-correction method to five GCMs under three SSP scenarios. This approach reduces runoff biases and allows reliable projection of future changes in river discharge and hydrological extremes for 2041–2070 relative to 1980–2014. Furthermore, the relative contributions of climate change and reservoir regulation to these shifts are quantitatively isolated. New hydrological insights for the region Results indicate that reservoir regulation dominates future flood changes with a reduction of −20.5% to −21.4%, largely offsetting the 13%–16.1% increase driven by climate change. However, this buffer is being outpaced by climate intensification, resulting in future regulated flood peaks that still exceed historical levels by 8.59%. Simultaneously, the basin will transition to a perennial high-flow state in the dry season that fundamentally homogenizes natural eco-hydrological conditions. Downstream tributaries emerge as the most volatile zones, facing the highest climate-driven intensification risk. These findings underscore the urgent need for a cohesive, basin-wide coordinated strategy to manage escalating residual risks under intensifying climate extremes.

title: Analysis of agricultural land exposure to Compound Dry-Heat Events in Northeast China
description: Publication date: June 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 65 Author(s): Xiaoxue Ma, Wandi Xu, Defeng Zheng, Ying Li, Ziying Liu, Jihao Liang, Jiachen Tan
abstract: Study region Northeast China (NEC) Study focus In the context of global climate change, frequent Compound Dry-Heat Events (CDHEs) severely threaten the sustainable agricultural development of the NEC. This study investigates the spatiotemporal evolution of CDHEs and their impacts on agricultural land exposure. We used high-resolution gridded meteorological data (1960–2022) and remote sensing land-use data (1992–2022), constructed a Bivariate Dry-Heat Index (BDHI) by coupling SPI and STI, and employed Sen's slope, Mann-Kendall test, kernel density estimation, dynamic degree model, gridded exposure assessment, and wavelet analysis to quantify CDHEs’ spatiotemporal patterns, agricultural land changes, and exposure driving mechanisms. New hydrological insights for the region CDHEs in the NEC exhibited a significant intensification trend, with annual occurrence days increasing from 70 to approximately 180 days and high-value areas expanding spatially. Agricultural land exposure presented a first decreasing then increasing pattern, with hotspots centered on the Greater Khingan Range; the area of high-exposure zones in 2010–2022 was 2.3 times that in the 1990s. Climatic factors accounted for 98.8% of exposure changes, significantly more than land use (0.9%) and their interaction (0.3%). This study provides a new methodological framework for agricultural climate risk assessment and scientific support for regional food security and climate change adaptation management.

title: Analysis and prediction of groundwater salinity on Yongxing Island using multiple machine learning models integrated with sparrow search algorithm
description: Publication date: June 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 65 Author(s): Chuan-An Xia, Xinyu Gao, Daning Li, Jiayun Li, Yasong Li, Bill X. Hu
abstract: Study region Yongxing Island (YI), Xuande Atoll, Sansha City, China. Study focus We explore the driving mechanism of temporal variation of Groundwater Salinity (GS) on YI using totally eleven types of monitoring factors. We develop a framework to accurately and efficiently predict GS on YI relying on integrating the Sparrow Search Algorithm (SSA) with machine learning models. Three kinds of hydrological events (i.e., Extreme Tide (ETEs), Strong Evapotranspiration (SEEs), and Heavy Rainfall (HREs) Events) are identified, analyzed, and simulated. The relative importance of various monitoring factors in predicting GS and therefore managing water resources is determined through factor ablation and Shapley Additive exPlanations analysis. New hydrological insights The dominant period of GS is 90 days, while that for Groundwater pressure and Temperature (GT) are 75.4 and 28.6 days, respectively, which indicate the complicated driving mechanism of temporal variation of GS. The numbers of SEEs, ETEs, and HREs identified on YI in 2019 are eleven, six, and five, respectively, suggesting the strong influences of evapotranspiration, tide, and rainfall on GS. SSA coupled with Long Short-Term Memory (SSA-LSTM) leads to overall the highest prediction accuracy of GS during the exemplary ETEs, SEEs, and HREs. GS itself is the most critical monitoring factor for achieving high prediction accuracy of GS through SSA-LSTM, followed by tide level and GT, revealing the significant role of evaporation in governing GS variation.

title: Incorporating empirical orthogonal function analysis into lumped hydrological models with grid data
description: Publication date: June 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 65 Author(s): Peng Jiang, Yubing Ou, Nana Zhang, Rongrong Zhang, Bin Yang, Changhai Tan, Simin Qu, Jiacuo DunZhu, Cizhu Danba, Rui Wu, Zhongbo Yu
abstract: Study region This study focuses on the Tuotuo River Basin (TRB), located in the headwater region of the Yangtze River. Study focus We proposed an Empirical Orthogonal Function (EOF)-based framework to aggregate spatially distributed precipitation data from the China Meteorological Forcing Dataset (CMFD) into a spatially weighted series for the HBV model, aiming to improve the simulation of seasonal flood peaks and hydrological processes in the TRB. New hydrological insights for the region Basin-scale precipitation is controlled mainly by a coherent large-scale pattern with strong topographic modulation. The EOF based weighted precipitation better reflects basin-scale precipitation concentration, while its slightly higher monthly medians and larger spring dispersion suggest enhanced sensitivity to spatial heterogeneity during the pre-monsoon period. The EOF-based framework significantly enhanced the simulation of seasonal flood peaks in the TRB, particularly in terms of timing and magnitude of high-flow events from May to October.

title: Assessing the accuracy of different open-source Digital Elevation Models (DEMs) in morphometric analysis of Kanchi River basin
description: Publication date: June 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 65 Author(s): Arun Mondal, Anupam Pandey, Souvik Mondal, Sananda Kundu, Thanh Nhan Duc Tran, Venkataraman Lakshmi
abstract: Study region The Kanchi river basin is located in India. Study focus The Digital Elevation Model (DEM) is an important input in morphometric analysis; however, the accuracy of DEMs has not been comprehensively assessed, particularly over the Kanchi River basin, India. Furthermore, very few studies have been conducted on newly released DEMs, e.g., NASA DEM. This study compares the vertical accuracy of publicly accessible 16 DEM products, with spatial resolutions ranging from 12 m to 90 m, using toposheet data as a reference. We also evaluate how accuracy changes with increasing elevation. Specifically, morphometric parameters calculated from these DEMs are compared, and the impact of DEM spatial resolution on these parameters is examined. Six statistical parameters (R2, NASH, ME, RMSE, NMSE, and PBIAS) are used to analyze DEM accuracy. New hydrological insights We found that (1) TanDEM-X (resolution of 12 m) and the ALOS DEM (i.e., AW3D; 30 m) performed best, with low RMSE values of 8.37 m and 8.66 m, respectively; (2) DEM accuracy decreases with increasing elevation, and the accuracy of low-resolution DEMs decreases more rapidly than that of high-resolution DEMs; (3) a significant difference in morphometric parameters was observed between low- and high-resolution DEM products; and (4) due to their detailed surface elevation and high vertical accuracy, high-resolution DEMs (TanDEM-X and AW3D) provide a better and more reliable estimation of basin morphometry.

title: Spatiotemporal characteristics of precipitation concentration over the Greater Mekong Subregion and the potential association with large-scale climate factors
description: Publication date: June 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 65 Author(s): Yawen Yang, Zizhen Dong, Ruowen Yang, Li Wang, Ruilong Liu, Letian Zheng, Xinda Shan
abstract: Study region The study area is the Greater Mekong Subregion (GMS), including Yunnan province of Southwest China, and Myanmar, Laos, Thailand, Cambodia, Vietnam. Study focus The spatiotemporal characteristics and potential climate drivers of precipitation concentration (PC) during 1981–2020 over the GMS are investigated in the study. PC is an important indicator that can reflect the extent of annual or seasonal precipitation in a region unevenly distributed and concentrated over time, and can also denote the period when the maximum precipitation occurs. Three PC indicators are examined including the precipitation concentration index (PCI), precipitation concentration degree (PCD), and precipitation concentration period (PCP). New hydrological insights for the region These three PC indicators present significantly interannual and interdecadal variations, with a distinct climatic feature of "concentrated gets more concentrated and earlier, and uniform gets more uniform and later" in the spatial distribution. These PC variations are strongly associated with changes in extreme precipitation over the GMS. More uniform precipitation distribution and earlier concentration period are associated with a significant increase in the frequency and intensity of extreme precipitation in areas of the GMS and vice versa. Further analysis indicates that the El Niño-Southern Oscillation on the interannual timescale and the Interdecadal Pacific Oscillation/Pacific Decadal Oscillation on the interdecadal timescale are the dominant climate drivers for PC variations over the GMS.

title: Radium isotope tracing reveals that submarine groundwater discharge is a key influencing factor for blue carbon balance and mangrove carbon storage in the southern waters of Jinhai Bay
description: Publication date: June 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 65 Author(s): Shengwen Liu, Qiaona Guo, Lingwei Xu, Yifa Chen, Jinhai Zhou, Lu Chao
abstract: Study region Jinhai Bay, situated in the coastal zone of Guangxi, southern China (21°23′N–21°39′N, 109°17′E–109°29′E). Study focus The objective of this study is to evaluate how submarine groundwater discharge (SGD) impacts the blue carbon balance in Jinhai Bay. An innovative equation has been formulated to quantify dissolved carbon loss in mangroves caused by SGD, incorporating mangrove area, and the rates of SGD and recirculated submarine groundwater discharge (RSGD), along with the variance in dissolved carbon levels between groundwater and coastal seawater to determine the net carbon loss flow. This study compares results with traditional methods to assess how SGD-driven carbon loss affects the accuracy of mangrove carbon storage estimates. New hydrological insight for the region: The SGD rate in the dry season of Jinhai Bay was 5.80 cm/d. Dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) and dissolved organic carbon (DOC) flux of SGD were 8.39 × 106 mol/d and 1.18 × 107 mol/d, which accounted for 50% and 69% of the total DIC and DOC sources in the study area, respectively. Additionally, the net dissolved carbon flux loss from Jinhai Bay mangrove ecosystem caused by SGD was estimated at 2.44 × 105 mol/d, representing 43% of mangrove primary productivity and 75% of sediment carbon burial flux. This study highlights that ignoring SGD-driven carbon loss overestimates mangrove carbon storage, emphasizing the necessity of integrating SGD into coastal blue carbon budget and mangrove carbon storage assessments.

title: A classified artificial intelligence model based on triple-attention mechanism and metaheuristic algorithm for monthly runoff prediction
description: Publication date: June 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 65 Author(s): Wenjie Liu, Zhongkai Feng, Wenjing Niu, Junjie Liu, Shenglan Jian, Benda Liang
abstract: Study region This study focuses on snowmelt-dominated basins in the Northern Hemisphere, including the Yenisei, Ob, Amur, and Yukon River basins, which are characterized by strong seasonality with snow accumulation in winter and rapid melt runoff during spring. Study focus This study proposes a triple-attention evolutionary AI model for monthly runoff forecasting in snowmelt-dominated basins. Multiple climate phenomenon indices are selected through maximal information coefficient analysis, and K-means clustering identifies distinct hydro-climatic patterns. For each cluster, an enhanced LSTM with multi-vector, predictor, and temporal attention mechanisms captures nonlinear climate-runoff relationships, with a cooperation search algorithm used to optimize clustering and model parameters. New hydrological insights for the region The proposed model demonstrates superior forecasting accuracy across the four snowmelt-dominated basins. For the Yenisei River with clustering number K= 5, it achieves testing NSE of 0.822, outperforming SVM (0.750) and RNN (0.718). The model reveals that antecedent runoff consistently exerts the strongest influence on monthly runoff, reflecting hydrological persistence, while climate indices show varying and compensatory effects across intra- and inter-annual timescales. Specifically, indices such as the Asia Polar Vortex Intensity and Pacific Subtropical High Ridge Position exhibit inverse relationships with runoff, indicating their compensatory roles in hydrological variability. The findings highlight the complex interactions between large-scale climate patterns and monthly runoff in high-latitude basins, supporting reliable runoff prediction and adaptive water management under climate change.

title: Lakeshore land use modulates microbial carbon metabolism: The role of hydrochemistry and DOM composition
description: Publication date: June 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 65 Author(s): Yuqing Lv, Jing Hu, Dengping Zhang, Wen Wang, Yunchuan Long, Juan Jiang, Shaoqi Zhou
abstract: Study region Caohai Lake, southwestern China. Study focus Lakeshore land use can modify dissolved organic matter (DOM), hydrochemistry, and microbially mediated carbon metabolism in lakes, yet these linkages remain insufficiently resolved. We investigated four functional zones in Caohai Lake: the urban lakeshore zone (CW), the urban-adjacent lake zone (CN), the wooded-meadow lakeshore zone (MW), and the wooded-meadow-adjacent lake zone (MN). Microbial communities, carbon-metabolism genes, DOM properties, and environmental variables were compared to determine how contrasting anthropogenic and natural lakeshore settings regulate lake carbon metabolism. New hydrological insights for the region Lakeshore land use strongly shaped microbial community structure and carbon-metabolism genes in Caohai Lake. The CW zone was affected by domestic sewage, exhibiting reduced abundance of bacteria and genes, and a simple network structure. In contrast, the CN, MN, and MW areas, which were far from the towns, had reduced environmental pressure, increased microbial community and gene abundance, and a more stable and complex network structure. DOM composition was the main factor influencing the differences in microorganisms and carbon metabolism genes. Specifically, humic-like fractions and high concentrations of DOC promoted the diversity of microbial communities and gene abundance. Water chemical ions such as Ca2 + , Mg2+, and HCO3 - regulate carbonate precipitation and inorganic carbon supply. The study revealed the effects and drivers of lakeshore land use change on lake microbiology and carbon metabolism.

title: Influence and source contribution of basin-scale nutrient loading on the water quality of the isolated inter-basin water diversion canal
description: Publication date: June 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 65 Author(s): Xizhi Nong, Kunting Luo, Lihua Chen, Jiahua Wei, Ronghui Li
abstract: Study region The Middle Route of the South-to-North Water Diversion Project (MR-SNWD) of China, including the main conveyance canal and its surrounding watershed river networks along the project route. Study focus In this study, we constructed a watershed-scale nitrogen and phosphorus load estimation model based on the SPAtially Referenced Regressions On Watershed attributes (SPARROW) framework, and explored how canal water quality, under conditions without direct point-source pollution input, responds to variations in watershed non-point source nutrient loads. New hydrological insights for the region The results show that total nitrogen (TN) and total phosphorus (TP) loads exhibit similar spatial distribution patterns across river reaches and sub-watersheds, with TN generally posing a higher risk than TP. Nutrient load hotspots are strongly associated with human activities, with cultivated land contributing 43.1% of TN and 41.0% of TP in D-T Basin, and livestock and poultry farming contributing 55.6% of TN and 56.8% of TP in S-Y-W Basin. Along the main canal, annual and monthly TN and TP loads generally increase from south to north, with higher loads in spring and frequent fluctuations in summer and autumn, indicating that non-point source pollution along the project route, particularly in central-northern regions and watershed boundary areas, requires heightened attention even in the absence of direct point-source inputs.

title: Research on future climate change and hydrological response in the Luanhe River Basin
description: Publication date: June 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 65 Author(s): Linhao Wang, Ting Zhang, Jiyang Tian, Jianzhu Li, Ping Feng
abstract: Study region Luanhe River Basin, CHINA Study focus This study constructed a SWAT model for the Luanhe River Basin and quantitatively assessed the simulation capability of precipitation and temperature in the basin using eight Global Climate Models (GCMs) from the CMIP6 dataset. Climate variable values are derived using a weighted multi-model ensemble approach. Meteorological data are downscaled and bias-corrected using the Delta-DCSI method and an improved Quantile Mapping (QM) method that retains trend signals. Subsequently, the calibrated SWAT model is used to predict changes in runoff, soil water, and evapotranspiration under three Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs) scenarios for the future. New hydrological insight for the region As the outlet control station of the Luanhe River Basin, the Panjiakou hydrological station yielded R2 and NSE values exceeding 0.81 during the calibration period (1962–1995) and 0.70 during the validation period (1996–2017), demonstrating the model's proficiency in capturing basin-scale hydrological processes. Consequently, the SWAT model, driven by bias-corrected meteorological data, was employed to simulate hydrological responses under future climate scenarios. The results indicate that projections across the three future scenarios indicate that precipitation and temperature follow an increasing trajectory, despite the presence of sharp interannual fluctuations in precipitation. Runoff, soil water, and evapotranspiration demonstrate fluctuating upward trends with substantial spatial differentiation. The most pronounced changes in hydro-meteorological elements occur under the SSP585 scenario, reaching their maximum increments in the long-term period. Furthermore, runoff, soil water, and evapotranspiration display similar spatial distribution patterns, being higher in the east and south and lower in the west and north.

title: Decreased precipitation intensifies hydrological drought in the largest river basin of the Tibetan Plateau
description: Publication date: June 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 65 Author(s): He Sun, Bowen Zheng, Qikai Sun
abstract: Study region The Yarlung Zangbo (YZ) basin, the largest river basin on the Tibetan Plateau, is a climatically complex international river that plays a critical role in regional water security while facing a high risk of extreme hydrometeorological drought. Study focus Hydrological droughts in cryospheric basins are governed by interactions between climate variability and glacier processes, yet their dominant drivers remain poorly constrained. This study combines the VIC-Glacier model with explainable machine learning techniques (XGBoost/RF coupled with SHAP) to investigate hydrological droughts during 1998–2020 and to quantify the relative contributions of climatic, cryospheric, and large-scale atmospheric drivers. New hydrological insights for the region Results revealed pronounced spatial heterogeneity in drought characteristics across YZ sub-basins. The upstream Nuxia (NX) basin experienced intensified meteorological drought (-0.04 per decade), with droughts concentrated in winter and spring. In contrast, the downstream NX-BXK sub-basin exhibited spatially extensive, multi-seasonal droughts despite higher glacier coverage, indicating strong hydrological sensitivity to precipitation variability. Hydrological droughts showed clear amplification relative to meteorological droughts, with greater severity and duration, particularly in the NX-BXK sub-basin where runoff declines exceeded precipitation reductions. Attribution results identify the Arctic Oscillation as the dominant driver (30–35%), followed by precipitation anomalies and precipitation-induced runoff. Glacier runoff played a minor role in drought occurrence (<5%) but reduced drought severity by 10–36% during drought events.

title: Impacts of ecological water replenishment on groundwater dynamics and urban safety: Insights from ground deformation in Beijing Yongding River area, China
description: Publication date: June 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 65 Author(s): Yujia Han, Mingliang Gao, Huili Gong, Min Shi, Huayu Guan, Yunxiao Liu, Jie Wang, Yun Pan, Zheng Chen
abstract: Study region This study investigates spatiotemporal ground deformation and groundwater responses in the Beijing reach of the Yongding River Basin, China, where ecological water replenishment (EWR) has been implemented to improve river–aquifer interaction and regional water sustainability. Study focus SBAS-InSAR deformation time series were integrated with groundwater-level observations to characterize subsidence–uplift dynamics under EWR-related hydrologic change. Seasonal–Trend decomposition using Loess (STL) and wavelet-based time–frequency analysis were applied to separate long-term deformation trends from seasonal and transient components and to diagnose changing periodicities and groundwater–deformation coupling. A station-level hydrogeological framework based on lithology, groundwater-yield zoning, and compressible-layer thickness was used to support interpretation of deformation recovery. New hydrological insights for the region A pronounced downstream hotspot occurs in the eastern Beijing reach, where persistent subsidence reaches 58.95 mm/year. Along Daxing Airport Line corridor, local subsidence approaches 30 mm/year, with cumulative displacement of about 200 mm, identifying a priority zone for monitoring. Deformation responses are spatially heterogeneous and temporally non-stationary, and groundwater–deformation coupling varies across sites and time windows. Compressible-layer thickness is a first-order control on uplift magnitude during groundwater recovery (Spearman ρ = 0.53, p = 0.001 across all stations; ρ = 0.73, p = 0.001 for direct polygon-intersection sites). Although EWR-related deformation remains limited at most analyzed locations, areas with thicker compressible deposits, stronger confinement, or sensitive infrastructure require enhanced monitoring and cautious replenishment management.

title: Operational flood forecasting with adaptive dual-correction bayesian model averaging in the Huai river basin
description: Publication date: June 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 65 Author(s): Sheng Jiang, Changkun Li, Jiejinhao Liu, Bingxi Huang, Huiming Zhang
abstract: Study region This study is conducted in the Huai River Basin (China), using observed flood events and corresponding hydraulic simulations to evaluate the applicability of the proposed framework for operational flood forecasting and uncertainty assessment. Study focus This study develops an Adaptive Dual-Correction Bayesian Model Averaging (ADC-BMA) framework for operational flood forecasting in the Huai River Basin, China. The framework addresses two key challenges: the time-varying nature of forecast residuals during flood events and the representation of predictive uncertainty across different hydrological variables. By integrating hydraulic simulations with dual residual correction and adaptive probabilistic fusion, it enables more reliable forecasting of both streamflow and water stage under dynamically evolving conditions. New hydrological insights for the region In the Huai River Basin, forecast uncertainty shows variable- and regime-dependent behaviour. During floods, streamflow between-model variance rises sharply to 0.6–0.9, indicating uncertainty driven by inflow and roughness perturbations. By contrast, water stage uncertainty is dominated by persistent within-model residuals rather than between-model variance. Overall errors reflect both time-varying residual behaviour and systematic bias. Even with degraded inputs (10 dB), predictive skill remains strong, reducing errors by 130–150 m3/s for streamflow and 0.5–0.6 m for water stage. Therefore, forecasting requires distinct uncertainty strategies for streamflow and stage.

title: Streamflow forecasting with a hybrid model integrating a distributed hydrological model and deep learning methods
description: Publication date: June 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 65 Author(s): Xiao Liang, Li Liu, Lu Ding, Haiting Gu, Lu Wang, Yuxue Guo, Yue-Ping Xu
abstract: Study region The upper Jiao River, located in eastern China, is a representative mountainous watershed that experiences frequent flooding. Study focus Accurate and reliable streamflow forecasting, particularly during flood events, remains a major challenge. This study proposes a hybrid ensemble streamflow forecasting model that integrates a physically based hydrological model with a deep learning model, coupled through multiple hydrological elements, including streamflow, rainfall, soil moisture and soil extent. The proposed model was compared against a benchmark hydrological model driven solely by rainfall predictions. The performance of the ensemble streamflow forecasts from the hybrid model was assessed using both deterministic and probabilistic metrics. In addition, the model’s effectiveness was evaluated across three different flood types, i.e. flash floods (FF), short-duration rainfall floods (SRF), long-duration rainfall floods (LRF) determined by a process-based classification method. New hydrological insights for the region The results demonstrate that the hybrid model effectively captures the rainfall-runoff processes, delivering reliable forecasts with lead times of up to 5 days. Compared to the benchmark hydrological model, the hybrid model substantially reduces underestimation error of flood peaks and volumes, yielding higher accuracy and lower uncertainty. Notably, the model shows the greatest improvement in mean forecast accuracy for FF, whereas the benchmark hydrological model exhibits the poorest performance among all the three flood types considered. These findings underscore the efficacy of hybrid modeling in improving the accuracy and reliability of flood forecasting, thereby supporting more effective early warning systems and reducing uncertainty during extreme rainfall and flood events.

title: Characterizing water distribution and flow patterns controlled by the Tan-Lu Fault zone in Anhui province
description: Publication date: June 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 65 Author(s): Dejian Wang, Jiazhong Qian, Guanqun Zhou, Lei Ma
abstract: Study region The Tan-Lu Fault zone in Anhui province, China. Study focus This study systematically analyzed the regulatory effect of fault zone on the distribution and runoff characteristics of regional shallow groundwater and river system, and revealed the control mechanism of the fault structure on the hydrological system. New hydrological insights for the region The findings indicate that drainage basins (Huaihe, Chaohu, Caizihu, and Wanhe) controlled by the Tan-Lu Fault zone in Anhui Province have differentiated shallow groundwater flow fields. Shallow groundwater in each drainage basin converges towards the low-lying basins formed by the fault zone and eventually flows into the main river system. Due to the influence of the fault zone, the aquifers structure of regional shallow groundwater has significant spatial heterogeneity characteristics. The Huaihe and Chaohu drainage basins are dominated by pore water in unconsolidated sedimentary rock with high water-yielding property; the Caizihu and Wanhe drainage basins are dominated by fracture water in bedrock with significant differentiation in water-yielding property. The activity of the Tan-Lu Fault zone has caused many rivers in the study area to exhibit a significant movement at the vertical intersection with the fault zone, having displacement distances ranging from 290 m to over 2000 m. The above studies systematically reveal the coupling relationship between fault structure and hydrological system, providing a scientific basis for regional water resource research.

title: Catchment clustering in Taiwan through comparative assessment of baseflow separation methods
description: Publication date: June 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 65 Author(s): Hsin-Yu Chen, Hsin-Fu Yeh
abstract: Study region 60 catchments, Taiwan Study focus This study presents catchment clustering based on reliable baseflow estimation, using long-term streamflow data (1949–2022) from widespread gauging stations across Taiwan. The reliable baseflow estimation is based on integrating the selection of seven separation methods (Lyne-Hollick, Chapman-Maxwell, Eckhardt, UKIH, Fixed, Sliding, and Local interval) and parameters. A sensitivity analysis was conducted on the filtering parameters, and an objective benchmark based on recession flow for baseflow estimation was employed to select optimal method–parameter combinations. In addition, assessing the influence of reservoirs on BFI ensures the representativeness of the selected catchments. Finally, catchments were classified using k-means clustering based on the seasonal BFI. New hydrological insights for the region The LH method (α=0.925) and the ECK method (α=0.925, BFImax=0.8) as optimal method–parameter combinations, achieving an NSE of 0.97 and 0.99, respectively. Most rivers in Taiwan are dominated by subsurface contributions, with about 60% of streamflow coming from subsurface sources especially in mountainous regions. However, hydrogeological maps indicate that these regions are generally unfavorable for substantial groundwater contributions. Moreover, BFI was found to be largely unaffected by hydraulic infrastructures. The 60 catchments were classified into 5 distinct groups, each characterized by unique BFI magnitudes and seasonal dynamics. These findings provide valuable insights for selecting separation method parameters, understanding the composition of streamflow and the spatial variability of catchment behaviors of each group in Taiwan.

title: Quantifying socioeconomic impacts of urban pluvial flooding using social media and SDGSAT-1 nighttime light data: A case study of Kunming, China
description: Publication date: June 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 65 Author(s): Xingyi Zhang, Yaxin Zhang, Yihan Wu, Maolin Zhang, Fei Zhao, Hangtian Pan, Zhenhua Zhong, Yongqi Sun, Xinrui Wang, Xiaoqing Zhao, Yang Shen
abstract: Study region This study focuses on Kunming, China—a city with complex terrain and recurrent waterlogging—where urban flooding threatens socioeconomic stability but conventional methods lack spatiotemporal granularity for nighttime impact assessment. Study focus This study presents a multi-source data fusion framework integrating geolocated Weibo posts and sub-10m SDGSAT-1 nighttime light (NTL) imagery to assess flood disasters. This framework identifies flood-prone areas and quantifies impacts with unprecedented spatial detail.
